  c(
    fit_zones_sf, aus_shp, prediction_region_sf,
    hmm_data, plague_hmm, plague_hmm_ppc, plague_hmm_pseudores,
    hmm_observation_model, hmm_transition_model,
    anchor_trap_success_threshold, anchor_burrow_threshold, anchor_trap_low_threshold, anchor_trap_low_min_effort,
    plague_risk_map, plague_risk_map_uncertainty, plague_build_up_map, plague_onset_map,

    min_temp_cold_days12_raster, soil_moisture_rolling_anomaly_raster_12, soil_moisture_rolling_anomaly_raster_36,

  gpp_rolling3_anomaly            = gpp_rolling_anomaly_raster_3,
  soil_moisture_anomaly           = soil_moisture_anomaly_raster,

  gpp_anomaly = "z-score", gpp_rolling6_anomaly = "z-score", gpp_rolling3_anomaly = "z-score",

  soil_moisture_rolling6_anomaly = "z-score", soil_moisture_anomaly = "z-score", prev_rain_anomaly = "z-score",
  gpp_rolling6 = "gC/m²/day", gpp_finescale = "gC/m²/day", gpp_finescale_survey = "gC/m²/day",

## A covariate's axis title: its readable name with its units, inside the name's own brackets where it has them.
axis_label_of <- function(v) {
  label <- label_of(v)
  unit <- ifelse(v %in% names(covariate_units), covariate_units[v], NA_character_)
  ifelse(is.na(unit), label, ifelse(endsWith(label, ")"), paste0(sub("\\)$", "", label), "; ", unit, ")"), paste0(label, " (", unit, ")")))
}

strip_as_axis_title <- theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.background = element_blank(),
                             strip.text.x.bottom = element_text(size = rel(1.2), margin = margin(t = 4, b = 4)),
                             ## Strip text isn't clipped to the strip's own box.

## The four estimated transitions (low -> plague and plague -> medium are ruled out).
transitions <- tibble::tibble(
  from  = c(1, 2, 2, 3),
  to    = c(2, 3, 1, 1),
  label = c("Low → medium", "Medium → plague", "Medium → low", "Plague → low")
)

## Hazard palette (calm sage to brick red), for line colours.
hazard_colors <- c("#3F5B45", "#7C8C43", "#C99A34", "#BE5F2C", "#7A2626")
## Probability maps: a linear scale diverging at 50% -- blue where a probability is under 50%, white at 50% and red
## above it (as on mouseforecast.com).
risk_scale <- scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", midpoint = 0.5, limits = c(0, 1),
                                   breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), labels = scales::percent, name = "Probability")

## Map layers in WGS84: national outline and fitted AE zones.
aus_sf <- st_as_sf(aus_shp) |> st_transform(4326)
fit_zones_ll <- st_transform(fit_zones_sf, 4326)
prediction_region_ll <- st_transform(prediction_region_sf, 4326)

## The four chew-card streams share every coefficient, so chewcard_count stands in for all four.
chewcard_streams <- c("chewcard_count", "chewcard_block2", "chewcard_block3", "chewcard_block4")

## AE zones (transitions) and adjusted AE zones (burrow/chew-card zone effects).
zone_levels <- levels(hmm_data$ae_zone)
adj_zone_levels <- levels(hmm_data$ae_zone_adj)
season_order <- c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring")
soil_colours <- c("cracking clay" = "#8c510a", "duplex/calcareous loam" = "#d8b365", "sandy earth" = "#5ab4ac")

## Mann-Whitney AUC: probability a positive case outranks a negative one.
auc_fn <- function(yes, no) {
  r <- rank(c(yes, no))
  (sum(r[seq_along(yes)]) - length(yes) * (length(yes) + 1) / 2) / (length(yes) * length(no))
}
fmt2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
pct <- function(x, acc = 0.1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = acc)
## One element of the model specification (_targets.R) written out as R code, for display in a code block that
## isn't run: a stream's list of family and terms, or a transition's vector of terms.
spec_code <- function(name, spec) {
  as_code <- function(v) if (length(v) == 1) paste0('"', v, '"') else paste0("c(\n", paste0('      "', v, '"', collapse = ",\n"), "\n    )")
  if (!is.list(spec)) return(c(paste0(name, " = c("), paste0('  "', spec, '"', c(rep(",", length(spec) - 1), "")), ")"))
  fields <- vapply(names(spec), function(f) {
    v <- spec[[f]]
    paste0("    ", f, " = ", if (is.list(v)) deparse1(v) else as_code(v))
  }, character(1))
  c(paste0(name, " = list("), paste0(fields, c(rep(",", length(fields) - 1), "")), ")")
}
## A code block for a knitted child: the lines, fenced as R code that isn't run.
code_block <- function(lines) c("```r", lines, "```", "")
## "a, b and c" for lists in the text.
and_join <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])

## The outline of a grid's mapped cells, traced around the cells themselves, so cells near the white middle of
## a diverging scale still show where the mapped area ends.
cell_outline <- function(df) {
  cells <- terra::rast(data.frame(x = df$x, y = df$y, value = 1)[!duplicated(df[, c("x", "y")]), ], type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326")
  sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(cells, dissolve = TRUE))
}
## A grid map of one value column, with the mapped area's outline and the national outline.
grid_map <- function(df, fill_col, fill_scale, title = NULL) {
  xr <- range(df$x); yr <- range(df$y); pad <- 0.6
  ggplot() +
    # geom_raster fills the regular 0.1 degree grid without the hairline gaps geom_tile leaves between rows.
    geom_raster(data = df, aes(x, y, fill = .data[[fill_col]])) +
    geom_sf(data = cell_outline(df), fill = NA, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    fill_scale +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(xr[1] - pad, xr[2] + pad), ylim = c(yr[1] - pad, yr[2] + pad), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 10.5))
}
## A single-layer raster as a data frame with a named value column.
raster_df <- function(r, name) {
  df <- as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- name
  df
}

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
)

```{r}
#| label: model-helpers
#| include: false

## One typical row of a data frame, for predictions at fixed conditions: each numeric column's median
## (0 if it has no values), each factor's most common level (levels kept), any other column's first
## value. rows restricts which rows the typical values come from (e.g. one stream's surveys).
typical_row <- function(data, rows = rep(TRUE, nrow(data))) {
  d <- as.data.frame(data)[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  out <- lapply(d, function(v) {
    if (is.numeric(v)) {
      m <- stats::median(v, na.rm = TRUE)
      return(if (is.na(m)) 0 else m)
    }
    if (is.factor(v)) {
      counts <- table(v)
      return(factor(if (sum(counts) > 0) names(which.max(counts)) else levels(v)[1], levels = levels(v)))
    }
    v[1]
  })
  ## The anchor column isn't a covariate.
  out$state <- NULL
  as.data.frame(out, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, optional = TRUE)
}

## hmmTMB's predict() with a 95% interval from 200 posterior draws, seeded so the report is reproducible.
predict_ci <- function(what, newdata) {
  set.seed(1)
  plague_hmm$predict(what = what, newdata = newdata, n_post = 200)
}

## The AE zone whose random deviations -- intercepts and zone slopes, summed over every transition -- are
## closest to zero, so its curves are closest to the pooled, zone-average curves.
re_all <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_re()[, 1]
zone_dev <- re_all[grepl("s\\(ae_zone\\)(:[a-z0-9_]+)?\\.[0-9]+$", names(re_all))]
dev_by_zone <- tapply(abs(zone_dev), as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", names(zone_dev))), sum)
reference_zone <- zone_levels[as.integer(names(which.min(dev_by_zone)))]
common_soil_group <- names(which.max(table(hmm_data$soil_group)))

## Typical conditions for transition predictions: every covariate at its median, the reference zone and
## the most common soil group.
base_transition_row <- typical_row(hmm_data)
base_transition_row$ae_zone <- factor(reference_zone, levels = zone_levels)
base_transition_row$soil_group <- factor(common_soil_group, levels = levels(hmm_data$soil_group))
base_transition_row$not_clay <- as.numeric(common_soil_group != "cracking clay")

## Variables in one transition's formula, a "_scaled" variable as its original covariate (curves vary
## covariates in real units and rescale them with the model's own constants).
transition_vars <- function(from, to) {
  f <- plague_hmm$hid()$formula()[from, to]
  if (is.na(f) || f == ".") return(character(0))
  vars <- setdiff(sub("_scaled$", "", all.vars(stats::as.formula(f))), c("ae_zone", "soil_group", "not_clay", "season"))
  ## Numeric covariates only (factors such as cropping_system are shown by their own panels), and not 0/1
  ## indicators such as post_plague, which are shown as factor levels.
  vars[vapply(vars, function(v) is.numeric(hmm_data[[v]]) && !is_indicator(v), logical(1))]
}
## Whether a numeric column only takes the values 0 and 1.
is_indicator <- function(v) is.numeric(hmm_data[[v]]) && all(stats::na.omit(unique(hmm_data[[v]])) %in% c(0, 1))
## Covariates whose slope differs off cracking clay in one transition's formula.
soil_interaction_vars <- function(from, to) {
  f <- plague_hmm$hid()$formula()[from, to]
  labels <- attr(stats::terms(stats::as.formula(f)), "term.labels")
  sub("_scaled$", "", unique(sub(":?not_clay:?", "", labels[grepl("not_clay", labels) & grepl(":", labels)])))
}

## Transition-prediction rows: typical conditions with one covariate set to each of values.
transition_newdata <- function(cv, values, zone = reference_zone, soil = common_soil_group) {
  nd <- base_transition_row[rep(1, length(values)), , drop = FALSE]
  nd[[cv]] <- values
  nd$ae_zone <- factor(zone, levels = zone_levels)
  nd$soil_group <- factor(soil, levels = levels(hmm_data$soil_group))
  nd$not_clay <- as.numeric(soil != "cracking clay")
  scale_covariates(nd, attr(plague_hmm, "covariate_scaling"))
}

```{r}
#| label: compute-forecast
#| include: false

## Season labels for a "<month>_<year>" covariate period, and the season after it (the forecast season).
period_seasons <- function(period) {
  info <- season_info(as.Date(paste(sub(".*_", "", period), sub("_.*", "", period), "15", sep = "-")))
  cov_season <- as.character(info$season)
  target <- season_order[(match(cov_season, season_order) %% 4) + 1]
  list(period = period, covariate_season = cov_season, covariate_year = info$year_adj,
       target_season = target, target_year = if (target == "Summer") info$year_adj + 1 else info$year_adj)
}

## The forecast: the grid hindcast's latest season, whose next-season state distribution is the forecast.
period_key <- function(p) as.integer(sub(".*_", "", p)) * 100 + as.integer(sub("_.*", "", p))
latest <- plague_hindcast[period_key(plague_hindcast$period) == max(period_key(plague_hindcast$period)), ]
forecast <- period_seasons(latest$period[1])

## Next season's state probabilities, inside the prediction region, and each cell's most likely state.
## (A raster mask on the forecast grid, rather than a point-in-polygon test the region's geometry fails under s2.)
region_mask <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(prediction_region_ll), plague_onset_map[[1]])
region_cells <- !is.na(terra::extract(region_mask, as.matrix(latest[, c("x", "y")]))[, 1])
forecast_cells <- latest[region_cells, ] |>
  filter(!is.na(next_1)) |>
  mutate(most_likely = factor(state_labels[max.col(cbind(next_1, next_2, next_3), ties.method = "first")], levels = state_labels),
         certainty = pmax(next_1, next_2, next_3))

## Next season's Pr(medium) and Pr(plague) by AE zone: mean, 90th percentile and maximum across cells.
risk_by_zone <- forecast_cells |>
  pivot_longer(c(next_2, next_3), names_to = "state", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(state = ifelse(state == "next_2", "Medium", "Plague")) |>
  group_by(ae_zone = as.character(ae_zone), state) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(p), q90 = stats::quantile(p, 0.9, names = FALSE), max = max(p), .groups = "drop")
top_zones <- risk_by_zone |> filter(state == "Plague") |> arrange(desc(mean)) |> slice_head(n = 2)

## What drives each cell's risk of a transition (low -> medium or medium -> plague): the transition's linear
## predictor (logit of its probability against staying put) split into one contribution per covariate --
## coefficients times values, its season, off-cracking-clay and zone-varying differences included -- plus a
## baseline (intercept, soil group and the zone's random intercept). Covariates are centred levels or
## anomalies, so a contribution reads as the push away from an average season. Checked against
## hmmTMB's own transition probabilities.
decompose_transition <- function(nd, from, to) {
  prefix <- paste0("S", from, ">S", to, ".")
  mats <- plague_hmm$hid()$make_mat(data = plague_hmm$obs()$data(), new_data = nd)
  ## This transition's rows of the stacked design (its intercept column is 1 there).
  rows <- which(mats$X_fe[, paste0(prefix, "(Intercept)")] == 1)
  fe <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()[, 1]
  re <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_re()[, 1]
  ## Each design column's covariate: the numeric variable in its term, or "baseline" for the
  ## intercept, soil group's own effect and the zone random intercept.
  column_covariate <- function(nm) {
    term <- substring(nm, nchar(prefix) + 1)
    if (startsWith(term, "s(ae_zone):")) return(sub("_scaled$", "", sub("^s\\(ae_zone\\):(.*)\\.[0-9]+$", "\\1", term)))
    parts <- strsplit(term, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    ## Soil group, season and cropping system only modify a slope or the baseline, so they're not covariates of their own.
    numeric_part <- parts[!startsWith(parts, "soil_group") & !startsWith(parts, "s(ae_zone)") & parts != "(Intercept)" & parts != "not_clay" &
                            !startsWith(parts, "season") & !startsWith(parts, "cropping_system")]
    if (length(numeric_part) == 0) "baseline" else sub("_scaled$", "", numeric_part)
  }
  ## This transition's fixed and random design columns, grouped by covariate.
  fe_cols <- colnames(mats$X_fe)[startsWith(colnames(mats$X_fe), prefix)]
  re_cols <- colnames(mats$X_re)[startsWith(colnames(mats$X_re), prefix)]
  fe_groups <- split(fe_cols, vapply(fe_cols, column_covariate, ""))
  re_groups <- split(re_cols, vapply(re_cols, column_covariate, ""))
  ## Each covariate's contribution: its columns times their coefficients, fixed and random.
  covariates <- union(names(fe_groups), names(re_groups))
  out <- lapply(covariates, function(cv) {
    v <- rep(0, length(rows))
    if (!is.null(fe_groups[[cv]])) v <- v + as.vector(as.matrix(mats$X_fe[rows, fe_groups[[cv]], drop = FALSE]) %*% fe[fe_groups[[cv]]])
    if (!is.null(re_groups[[cv]])) v <- v + as.vector(as.matrix(mats$X_re[rows, re_groups[[cv]], drop = FALSE]) %*% re[re_groups[[cv]]])
    v
  })
  names(out) <- covariates
  as.data.frame(out, check.names = FALSE)
}
forecast_grid <- build_risk_grid_newdata(plague_hmm, covariate_rasters, prediction_region_sf, forecast$period)
forecast_tpm <- plague_hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = forecast_grid$newdata)
## Each cell's contributions for one transition, with its probability; they must add up to hmmTMB's own
## log(Pr(transition) / Pr(staying put)).
transition_drivers <- function(from, to) {
  contributions <- decompose_transition(forecast_grid$newdata, from, to)
  stopifnot(max(abs(rowSums(contributions) - log(forecast_tpm[from, to, ] / forecast_tpm[from, from, ]))) < 1e-6)
  tibble::tibble(ae_zone = as.character(forecast_grid$newdata$ae_zone), risk = forecast_tpm[from, to, ]) |>
    bind_cols(contributions)
}
forecast_drivers <- list(`Low → medium` = transition_drivers(1, 2), `Medium → plague` = transition_drivers(2, 3))
```

```{r}
#| label: compute-transitions
#| include: false

## Each covariate varied over its 5th-95th percentile, others typical, with 95% intervals, for every
## transition it enters.
transition_curves <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(transition_vars(from, to), function(cv) {
    values <- seq(stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 40)
    p <- predict_ci("tpm", transition_newdata(cv, values))
    tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = cv, value = values,
                   mle = p$mle[from, to, ], lcl = p$lcl[from, to, ], ucl = p$ucl[from, to, ])
  })
})

## Effect sizes: each transition probability at the covariate's 10th and 90th percentiles, others typical.
effect_sizes <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(transition_vars(from, to), function(cv) {
    values <- stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], c(0.1, 0.9), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
    p <- plague_hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = transition_newdata(cv, values))
    tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = cv, low = p[from, to, 1], high = p[from, to, 2])
  })
}) |>
  mutate(change = high - low)

## The strongest driver of one transition, for the Summary.
top_driver <- function(tr) {
  e <- filter(effect_sizes, transition == tr) |> arrange(desc(abs(change)))
  paste0(tolower(label_of(e$covariate[1])), " (", if (e$change[1] > 0) "+" else "", round(100 * e$change[1]), " points from its 10th to 90th percentile)")
}

## The full transition matrix in a typical season (every covariate at its median, reference zone and
## soil group), with 95% intervals, and the average time spent in each state it implies.
typical_tpm <- predict_ci("tpm", transition_newdata("min_temp", stats::median(hmm_data$min_temp)))
typical_rates <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  tibble::tibble(Transition = label, p = typical_tpm$mle[from, to, 1], lcl = typical_tpm$lcl[from, to, 1], ucl = typical_tpm$ucl[from, to, 1])
})
## Average stay in each state: one over the chance of leaving it each season.
stay_seasons <- 1 / (1 - diag(typical_tpm$mle[, , 1]))
names(stay_seasons) <- state_labels
```

```{r}
#| label: compute-observations
#| include: false

## The observation term specification: each stream's main parameter and the hmm_data columns that hold
## its observations.
stream_info <- tibble::tribble(
  ~spec,          ~param,  ~stream,          ~stream_label,
  "trap_count",   "mean",  "trap_count",     "Live traps: captures per 100 trap-nights",
  "burrow_count", "mean",  "burrow_count",   "Active burrows per 100 m transect",
  "chewcard",     "prob",  "chewcard_count", "Chew cards: probability a card is chewed"
)
## Rows with each stream's surveys (any of the four chew-card blocks for chew cards).
stream_observed <- function(stream) {
  if (stream == "chewcard_count") Reduce(`|`, lapply(chewcard_streams, function(s) !is.na(hmm_data[[s]]))) else !is.na(hmm_data[[stream]])
}
## Typical conditions per stream (from that stream's own surveys), with search effort set to 100 trap-nights
## or 100 m of transect so means read per unit of effort.
stream_base_row <- function(stream) {
  row <- typical_row(hmm_data, stream_observed(stream))
  row$log_trap_effort <- log(100)
  row$log_burrow_metres_searched <- log(100)
  row
}

## How strongly each stream separates the states: the model's expected value in each state at every one
## of that stream's actual surveys (their own season, crop, soil, region and effort), averaged over the
## surveys, with the 10th-90th percentile across surveys as the spread from survey conditions, and the
## chance a survey finds nothing (zero count). Averaging over real surveys avoids the unrepresentative
## combination a single "typical" survey (each factor's most common level) can make. Trap and burrow means
## are scaled to 100 trap-nights and 100 m of transect; chew cards are the probability a card is chewed.
stream_contrast <- purrr::pmap_dfr(stream_info, function(spec, param, stream, stream_label) {
  rows <- which(!is.na(hmm_data[[stream]]))
  par <- plague_hmm$obs()$par(t = rows)
  stream_rows <- startsWith(rownames(par), paste0(stream, "."))
  ## Each survey's expected value in each state, per unit of effort where the stream has an offset.
  per_unit <- switch(stream, trap_count = 100 / hmm_data$trap_effort[rows],
                     burrow_count = 100 / hmm_data$burrow_metres_searched[rows], 1)
  value <- sweep(par[paste0(stream, ".", param), , , drop = TRUE], 2, per_unit, "*")
  ## Probability of a zero from the stream's own family, at each survey's fitted parameters in each state.
  pdf <- plague_hmm$obs()$dists()[[stream]]$pdf()
  pr_zero <- sapply(seq_along(state_labels), function(k) {
    mean(apply(par[stream_rows, k, , drop = FALSE], 3, function(pp) {
      names(pp) <- sub(paste0("^", stream, "\\."), "", rownames(par)[stream_rows])
      do.call(pdf, c(list(x = 0), as.list(pp)))
    }))
  })
  ## Summaries computed before the tibble, whose own "value" column would otherwise shadow the matrix.
  mean_value <- rowMeans(value)
  low_value  <- apply(value, 1, stats::quantile, 0.1)
  high_value <- apply(value, 1, stats::quantile, 0.9)
  tibble::tibble(Stream = stream_label, State = state_labels,
                 value = mean_value, lcl = low_value, ucl = high_value,
                 pr_zero = pr_zero, n_surveys = length(rows))
})
## Each state's expected value relative to the low state, per stream.
stream_ratio <- function(stream_label, state) {
  d <- filter(stream_contrast, Stream == stream_label)
  d$value[d$State == state] / d$value[d$State == "Low"]
}
```

```{r}
#| label: compute-detection
#| include: false

## Crop stages in growth order, for the detection-effect panels.
crop_stage_order <- c("sown", "seedling", "vegetative", "flowering", "ripening", "stubble", "not recorded")

## Detection effects: each stream's observation terms, one panel per covariate, at typical conditions
## for that stream, in each of the three states, with 95% intervals. Panels come from the specification itself: a factor
## shows each level; a numeric covariate a curve over its 5th-95th percentile; a two-way interaction is
## drawn as the first variable split by the second (e.g. season by cropping system).
detection_panels <- function(stream_spec) {
  terms_vec <- stream_spec[[setdiff(names(stream_spec), c("family", "state_specific", "tied_states"))[1]]]
  ## Offsets and the intercept aren't detection effects.
  terms_vec <- terms_vec[!grepl("^offset\\(", terms_vec) & terms_vec != "1"]
  labels <- attr(stats::terms(stats::as.formula(paste("~", paste(terms_vec, collapse = " + ")))), "term.labels")
  ## Survey-date harmonics (e.g. rapid_sin1 ... rapid_cos2) are one effect -- detection through the year -- so
  ## they become a single day-of-year panel.
  harmonic <- grepl("_(sin|cos)[12]", labels)
  timing_vars <- unique(sub("_(sin|cos)[12]$", "_doy", regmatches(labels[harmonic], regexpr("[a-z]+_(sin|cos)[12]", labels[harmonic]))))
  ## The panel is split by cropping system only where the harmonics interact with it (a curve per system, e.g.
  ## burrows); with a cropping-system main effect alone (e.g. traps), the curve is shared and cropping system
  ## gets a panel of its own.
  timing_by <- if (any(harmonic & grepl(":", labels, fixed = TRUE) & grepl("cropping_system", labels, fixed = TRUE))) "cropping_system" else NA_character_
  labels <- labels[!harmonic]
  pairs <- strsplit(labels[grepl(":", labels)], ":", fixed = TRUE)
  ## Soil indicators are always the split, whichever order R gives the interaction's variables in.
  pairs <- lapply(pairs, function(p) if (p[1] %in% c("cracking_clay", "not_clay")) rev(p) else p)
  ## Variables drawn as the split of an interaction (or of the day-of-year panel) get no panel of their own.
  partners <- c(vapply(pairs, `[`, "", 2), if (length(timing_vars) > 0 && !is.na(timing_by)) timing_by)
  mains <- setdiff(labels[!grepl(":", labels)], partners)
  c(lapply(timing_vars, function(v) list(var = v, by = timing_by)),
    lapply(pairs, function(p) list(var = p[1], by = p[2])),
    lapply(setdiff(mains, vapply(pairs, `[`, "", 1)), function(v) list(var = v, by = NA_character_)))
}
## A survey's day-of-year harmonics, recomputed from its day of year (as in r/e_build_hmm_data.R), so a
## prediction row's date and harmonics always agree.
set_survey_harmonics <- function(nd) {
  for (prefix in c("rapid", "trap")) {
    doy <- nd[[paste0(prefix, "_doy")]]
    if (is.null(doy)) next
    nd[[paste0(prefix, "_sin1")]] <- sin(2 * pi * doy / 365.25)
    nd[[paste0(prefix, "_cos1")]] <- cos(2 * pi * doy / 365.25)
    nd[[paste0(prefix, "_sin2")]] <- sin(4 * pi * doy / 365.25)
    nd[[paste0(prefix, "_cos2")]] <- cos(4 * pi * doy / 365.25)
  }
  nd
}
detection_effects <- purrr::pmap_dfr(stream_info, function(spec, param, stream, stream_label) {
  base <- stream_base_row(stream)
  observed <- stream_observed(stream)
  rows <- purrr::map_dfr(detection_panels(hmm_observation_model[[spec]]), function(pnl) {
    raw_var <- sub("_scaled$", "", pnl$var)
    ## x values: each factor level seen in this stream's surveys, or a numeric grid in real units.
    x_values <- if (endsWith(pnl$var, "_doy")) {
      ## The whole year, weekly, for the day-of-year panel.
      seq(1, 365, by = 7)
    } else if (is.factor(hmm_data[[pnl$var]])) {
      observed_levels <- levels(droplevels(hmm_data[[pnl$var]][observed]))
      ## Crop stages in growth order rather than alphabetically.
      if (all(observed_levels %in% crop_stage_order)) intersect(crop_stage_order, observed_levels) else observed_levels
    } else {
      seq(stats::quantile(hmm_data[[raw_var]][observed], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
          stats::quantile(hmm_data[[raw_var]][observed], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 25)
    }
    ## Split values: a factor's levels, or a numeric indicator's values (e.g. cracking_clay 0 / 1).
    by_values <- if (is.na(pnl$by)) NA_character_ else if (is.factor(hmm_data[[pnl$by]])) levels(droplevels(hmm_data[[pnl$by]][observed])) else
      as.character(sort(unique(hmm_data[[pnl$by]][observed])))
    tidyr::expand_grid(x = as.character(x_values), by = by_values) |>
      mutate(panel = axis_label_of(raw_var), var = pnl$var, raw_var = raw_var, by_var = pnl$by,
             numeric = !is.factor(hmm_data[[pnl$var]]))
  })
  ## One prediction row per x (and split) value, everything else typical.
  nd <- base[rep(1, nrow(rows)), , drop = FALSE]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
    if (rows$numeric[i]) nd[[rows$raw_var[i]]][i] <- as.numeric(rows$x[i]) else nd[[rows$var[i]]][i] <- rows$x[i]
    if (!is.na(rows$by_var[i])) nd[[rows$by_var[i]]][i] <- if (is.numeric(hmm_data[[rows$by_var[i]]])) as.numeric(rows$by[i]) else rows$by[i]
  }
  for (v in names(nd)) if (is.factor(hmm_data[[v]])) nd[[v]] <- factor(as.character(nd[[v]]), levels = levels(hmm_data[[v]]))
  nd <- set_survey_harmonics(nd)
  nd <- scale_covariates(nd, attr(plague_hmm, "covariate_scaling"))
  p <- predict_ci("obspar", nd)
  par_name <- paste0(stream, ".", param)
  ## Trap captures per 100 trap-nights and burrows per 100 m (effort set to 100 above); chew cards per
  ## card. One copy of the rows per state.
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(state_labels), function(k) {
    rows |>
      mutate(Stream = stream_label, param = param, State = factor(state_labels[k], levels = state_labels),
             mle = p$mle[par_name, k, ], lcl = p$lcl[par_name, k, ], ucl = p$ucl[par_name, k, ])
  })
}) |>
  ## Whether each panel's effect is shared by every state: on the link scale (log for counts, logit for the
  ## chew-card probability), a shared term moves each state's curve by the same amount, so every state's
  ## curve minus its own mean is identical. A state-specific term (e.g. a per-state smooth) isn't.
  mutate(link_value = ifelse(param == "prob", stats::qlogis(mle), log(mle))) |>
  group_by(Stream, panel, State) |>
  mutate(shape = link_value - mean(link_value)) |>
  group_by(Stream, panel, x, by) |>
  mutate(spread = max(shape) - min(shape)) |>
  group_by(Stream, panel) |>
  mutate(tied = max(spread) < 1e-6) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-link_value, -shape, -spread)
## Shared panels are drawn once, in the low state, in this colour; state-specific panels keep a colour per state.
shared_label <- "Shared by all states (low state shown)"
detection_colours <- c(state_colours, setNames("grey25", shared_label))
## The rows to draw: shared panels in the low state only, relabelled; state-specific panels in every state.
detection_rows <- function(d) {
  d |>
    filter(!tied | State == state_labels[1]) |>
    mutate(State = factor(ifelse(tied, shared_label, as.character(State)), levels = names(detection_colours)))
}
## Short names for each stream's subsection.
stream_short <- c("Live traps", "Active burrows", "Chew cards")
names(stream_short) <- stream_info$stream_label

## One stream's categorical detection terms (factors, and factor-by-factor interactions): each level's
## expected value -- once, in the low state, for a term shared by all states, or in each state (colour) for
## a state-specific one -- a split variable (e.g. cropping system) by point shape. Log scale.
plot_detection_categorical <- function(stream_label) {
  d <- filter(detection_effects, Stream == stream_label, !numeric) |>
    detection_rows() |>
    mutate(split = ifelse(is.na(by), "none", paste0(label_of(by_var), ": ", by)),
           ## x categories keyed by panel, so each panel keeps its own level order.
           x_key = factor(paste(panel, x, sep = "|"), levels = unique(paste(panel, x, sep = "|"))))
  ggplot(d, aes(x_key, mle, colour = State, shape = split, group = interaction(State, split))) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 0.22) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = detection_colours, name = NULL, limits = force) +
    ## Unsplit panels are drawn but left out of the shape legend.
    scale_shape_discrete(breaks = setdiff(unique(d$split), "none"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(k) sub("^.*\\|", "", k)) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = wrap_title(paste(stream_label, "(log scale)"))) +
    strip_as_axis_title +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, size = 7.5), legend.position = "top", legend.direction = "vertical")
}
## Line types for split levels: solid for unsplit ("none"), a different broken line for every other level.
split_linetypes <- function(split) {
  levels_split <- setdiff(unique(split), "none")
  c(none = "solid", setNames(rep(c("dashed", "dotted", "dotdash", "longdash", "twodash", "12345678"), length.out = length(levels_split)), levels_split))
}
## One stream's numeric detection terms: one curve for a shared term (low state), or a curve per state
## (colour) for a state-specific one; a split variable (e.g. soil group) by line type; log scale as above.
plot_detection_numeric <- function(stream_label) {
  d <- filter(detection_effects, Stream == stream_label, numeric) |>
    detection_rows() |>
    mutate(split = ifelse(is.na(by), "none", paste0(label_of(by_var), ": ", by)))
  ggplot(d, aes(as.numeric(x), mle, colour = State, fill = State, linetype = split, group = interaction(State, split))) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), colour = NA, alpha = 0.1) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = detection_colours, name = NULL, limits = force) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = detection_colours, name = NULL, limits = force) +
    ## Unsplit curves solid; each split level its own broken line, so no split level looks like an unsplit curve.
    scale_linetype_manual(values = split_linetypes(d$split), breaks = setdiff(unique(d$split), "none"), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = wrap_title(paste(stream_label, "(log scale)"))) +
    strip_as_axis_title +
    ## Legend entries stacked, so long split labels aren't cut off at the figure's width.
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.direction = "vertical")
}

## Smoothed state probabilities (given each paddock's full survey history and anchors).
state_probs <- plague_hmm$state_probs()
colnames(state_probs) <- state_labels
season_mid_month <- c(Summer = 1L, Autumn = 4L, Winter = 7L, Spring = 10L)
panel_dates <- as.Date(paste(hmm_data$year_adj, season_mid_month[as.character(hmm_data$season)], "15", sep = "-"))
surveyed <- !is.na(hmm_data$trap_count) | !is.na(hmm_data$burrow_count) | !is.na(hmm_data$chewcard_count)
```

```{r}
#| label: compute-skill
#| include: false

## Hindcast skill (state-mean summary).
hindcast_scores <- filter(plague_hindcast_scores$scores, stat == "mean")
get_hindcast <- function(predictor_name, era_name, col = "auc_within") {
  hindcast_scores[[col]][hindcast_scores$predictor == predictor_name & hindcast_scores$era == era_name]
}

## Hindcast skill by state: AUC of each state's own flagged against unflagged years, before 2013.
state_skill <- plague_hindcast_scores$state_year |>
  filter(era == "hindcast", !is.na(flag)) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(Flagged = sum(flag), Years = n(),
            `Onset, one year ahead` = hindcast_auc(onset_lead_mean, flag),
            `Onset, same year` = hindcast_auc(onset_mean, flag),
            Occupancy = hindcast_auc(occupancy_mean, flag), .groups = "drop")
skilled_states <- state_skill$state[state_skill$`Onset, one year ahead` >= 0.75]
weak_states <- state_skill$state[state_skill$`Onset, one year ahead` < 0.6]

## Residual calibration and posterior-predictive statistics outside the simulated range.
pr_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(plague_hmm_pseudores, function(x, nm) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  tibble::tibble(Stream = nm, n = length(x), Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x), `% |z|>2` = 100 * mean(abs(x) > 2))
})
ppc_summary <- plague_hmm_ppc$simulated |>
  group_by(statistic) |>
  summarise(sim_mean = mean(simulated), sim_lo = quantile(simulated, 0.025), sim_hi = quantile(simulated, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(plague_hmm_ppc$observed, by = "statistic") |>
  mutate(inside = observed >= sim_lo & observed <= sim_hi)
ppc_outside <- ppc_summary$statistic[!ppc_summary$inside]
ppc_label <- function(stat) {
  stream <- c(trap_count = "trap", burrow_count = "burrow", chewcard_count = "chew-card")[sub(":.*", "", stat)]
  what <- dplyr::recode(sub(".*: ", "", stat), mean = "mean", SD = "SD", `Pr(0)` = "share of zeros", `Pr(10)` = "share of fully chewed sessions")
  paste(stream, what)
}

## Panel size, anchors and the mapped plague seasons.
n_rows     <- nrow(hmm_data)
n_paddocks <- n_distinct(hmm_data$ID)
fit_states <- sort(unique(hmm_data$aus_state))
anchor_counts <- table(factor(hmm_data$state, levels = c("3", "2", "2,3", "1,2", "1")))
mapped_seasons <- recent_plague_maps |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(season, year) |>
  arrange(year, match(season, season_order))
first_mapped_year <- min(mapped_seasons$year)

## Each state's mean probability by season, across all paddock-seasons.
season_shares <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(state_labels), function(k) {
  tibble::tibble(State = state_labels[k], season = hmm_data$season, p = state_probs[, k])
}) |>
  group_by(State, season) |>
  summarise(p = mean(p), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(State = factor(State, levels = state_labels), season = factor(season, levels = season_order))
```

## Summary

- **Current forecast.** For `r forecast$target_season` `r forecast$target_year` (from `r forecast$covariate_season` `r forecast$covariate_year` covariates), the chance of plague is highest in `r top_zones$ae_zone[1]` (zone mean `r pct(top_zones$mean[1])`) and `r top_zones$ae_zone[2]` (`r pct(top_zones$mean[2])`). The most likely state is medium in `r pct(mean(forecast_cells$most_likely == "Medium"))` of the prediction region and plague in `r pct(mean(forecast_cells$most_likely == "Plague"))`.
- **Three states.** Populations build up from low to medium when conditions turn good, become a plague after a sharp swing from dry to wet (rainfall whiplash) unless their zone came out of a plague within the last year, and fall back to low from either. In a typical season a paddock stays low for about `r round(stay_seasons[["Low"]], 1)` seasons, medium for `r round(stay_seasons[["Medium"]], 1)` and plague for `r round(stay_seasons[["Plague"]], 1)`.
- **What drives each step.** Building up responds most to `r top_driver("Low → medium")`; becoming a plague to `r top_driver("Medium → plague")`; a build-up fading to `r top_driver("Medium → low")`; and a plague ending to `r top_driver("Plague → low")`.
- **What the surveys say.** Against the low state, expected trap catches are `r round(stream_ratio(stream_info$stream_label[1], "Medium"), 1)` times higher in the medium state and `r round(stream_ratio(stream_info$stream_label[1], "Plague"), 1)` times in plague; burrow counts `r round(stream_ratio(stream_info$stream_label[2], "Medium"), 1)` and `r round(stream_ratio(stream_info$stream_label[2], "Plague"), 1)` times.
- **Forecast skill varies by region.** On recorded plague years before 2013, which the model never saw, one-year-ahead onset risk separates plague from non-plague years well in `r and_join(skilled_states)` (AUC ≥ 0.75)`r if (length(weak_states) > 0) paste0(" but poorly in ", and_join(weak_states), " (AUC < 0.6)") else ""`; the overall within-state AUC is `r fmt2(get_hindcast("onset_lead", "hindcast"))`.
- **Model checks.** Randomised residuals have means `r fmt2(min(pr_summary$Mean))` to `r fmt2(max(pr_summary$Mean))` and SDs `r fmt2(min(pr_summary$SD))` to `r fmt2(max(pr_summary$SD))`. `r if (length(ppc_outside) > 0) paste0("Data simulated from the model match the real data except for the ", and_join(ppc_label(ppc_outside)), ".") else "Data simulated from the model match every checked statistic."`
- **Data.** `r format(n_rows, big.mark = ",")` paddock-seasons across `r n_paddocks` paddocks in `r length(fit_states)` states; `r format(anchor_counts[["3"]], big.mark = ",")` anchored to plague from `r nrow(mapped_seasons)` hand-mapped plague seasons since `r first_mapped_year`, `r format(anchor_counts[["2"]] + anchor_counts[["2,3"]], big.mark = ",")` ruled out of the low state by high trap or burrow counts, and `r format(sum(hmm_data$trap_low), big.mark = ",")` well-trapped sessions with low trap success ruled out of plague.

## How the model works

```{=html}

<svg viewBox="0 0 980 560" role="img" aria-label="Diagram of the three-state seasonal hidden Markov model: low, medium and plague hidden states, with transitions low to medium, medium to plague, medium to low and plague to low each driven by its own covariates; each season's hidden state emits three conditionally independent observation streams (trap_count, burrow_count, chewcard_count)." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;font-family:inherit;">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arrowN" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor" />
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <text x="50" y="26" font-size="13" font-weight="600" fill="currentColor">PROCESS MODEL — hidden-state transitions, one season to the next</text>

  <circle cx="180" cy="150" r="42" fill="#3F5B45" fill-opacity="0.18" stroke="#3F5B45" stroke-width="1.8" />
  <text x="180" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="600" fill="currentColor">Low</text>
  <circle cx="490" cy="150" r="42" fill="#C99A34" fill-opacity="0.18" stroke="#C99A34" stroke-width="1.8" />
  <text x="490" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="600" fill="currentColor">Medium</text>
  <circle cx="800" cy="150" r="42" fill="#7A2626" fill-opacity="0.18" stroke="#7A2626" stroke-width="1.8" />
  <text x="800" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="600" fill="currentColor">Plague</text>

  <path d="M 222 138 L 446 138" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" fill="none" marker-end="url(#arrowN)" />

<figcaption>The hidden low / medium / plague state forms a Markov chain across seasons (top): each estimated transition has its own covariates, set by the season's conditions. Each season's state generates up to three observation streams (bottom). Most paddock-seasons observe one or two streams, or none; the state is then carried through by the transitions. Every term is listed in the Appendix.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

- **States and time step.** Three hidden states (low, medium, plague), one time series per paddock, one step per season; the initial distribution is the stationary one.
- **Families.** Trap and burrow counts are negative binomial; chew cards are beta-binomial, which lets cards within a session be chewed together. The beta-binomial comes from the patched hmmTMB build pinned in `renv.lock`.
- **Every term** is listed in the Appendix's specification tables, read from `_targets.R`; why each was chosen, and what was tried and left out, is in `r/e_fit_plague_hmm.R`.

### Data and anchoring

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data

## Surveys per state: paddocks, paddock-seasons, paddock-seasons with each observation stream, and anchors.
hmm_data |>
  group_by(State = aus_state) |>
  summarise(Paddocks = n_distinct(ID), `Paddock-seasons` = n(),
            `Live-trap` = sum(!is.na(trap_count)), `Active burrow` = sum(!is.na(burrow_count)),
            `Chew card` = sum(!is.na(chewcard_count)),
            Plague = sum(state %in% "3"), Medium = sum(state %in% "2"), `Medium or plague` = sum(state %in% "2,3"),
            `Low or medium` = sum(state %in% "1,2"), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(Paddocks)) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = -State) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Paddock-seasons surveyed by", columns = c(`Live-trap`, `Active burrow`, `Chew card`)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Paddock-seasons anchored to", columns = c(Plague, Medium, `Medium or plague`, `Low or medium`)) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

Each paddock is one time series of seasons from `r min(hmm_data$year_adj)` to `r max(hmm_data$year_adj)`, the years every covariate covers. Seasons without a survey stay in the panel with no observations, and repeat visits within a season are reduced to the first visit. `"Qld Central"` is excluded, having no surveys since 2008 and no plague anchors.

**Anchoring** fixes what is known about the hidden state, as a set of allowed states (`r/e_build_hmm_data.R`):

- **Plague maps.** From hand-digitised plague extents for each mapped season since `r first_mapped_year`, a paddock-season inside a mapped extent is anchored to plague. Outside the extents, it is anchored to "low or medium" only in seasons with no plague mapped in its region (WA or the eastern states); otherwise the model estimates its state. The two seasons before a plague anchor are left unanchored, since a plague is rarely confirmed the season it begins (`r/c_anchor_plague_state.R`).
- **High survey counts.** Trap success above `r anchor_trap_success_threshold` captures per 100 trap-nights, or more than `r anchor_burrow_threshold` active burrows per 100 m transect, rules out the low state: such a season is "medium or plague", or "medium" if the maps say it isn't plague.
- **Low trap success.** Trap success below `r anchor_trap_low_threshold` captures per 100 trap-nights, from a session of at least `r anchor_trap_low_min_effort` trap-nights, rules out the plague state: such a season is "low or medium", or "medium" with high burrow counts. It doesn't fix the low state, since mice can be hard to trap when food is plentiful and a building-up population can trap poorly. Where it contradicts a mapped plague, the season is left unanchored. Low burrow counts aren't used, since burrows are hard to see at some times and places; nor are chew cards, which relate less reliably to density. Between the two trap thresholds, and for smaller sessions, traps don't anchor the state.

```{r}
#| label: fig-anchor-maps
#| fig-cap: "The hand-digitised plague extents used as anchors, one panel per mapped season."
#| out-width: "100%"

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root_path, recent_plague_maps_map))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-state-seasons
#| fig-cap: "Mean probability of each state by season across all paddock-seasons. A flat line means the state isn't tracking the annual cycle of mouse activity, which the detection terms are there to absorb."
#| fig-asp: 0.45

ggplot(season_shares, aes(season, p, colour = State, group = State)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = state_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Season", y = "Mean probability") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Detection submodels

Each survey type (stream) has its own observation submodel: its count given the season's hidden state, with detection terms for the conditions of the survey. The table compares what each stream records in each state, averaged over its real surveys; each subsection below then gives the stream's specification and its estimated detection effects.


```{r}
#| label: tbl-stream-contrast

## Each stream's expected value in each state at typical conditions, and the chance of finding nothing.
stream_contrast |>
  mutate(digits = ifelse(grepl("probability", Stream), 3, 2),
         Expected = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f-%.", digits, "f)"), value, lcl, ucl),
         `× low state` = sprintf("%.1f×", value / value[State == "Low"][1]),
         `Pr(nothing found)` = pct(pr_zero, 1),
         .by = Stream) |>
  mutate(State = factor(State, levels = state_labels)) |>
  select(Stream, State, Expected, `× low state`, `Pr(nothing found)`) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Stream") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Expected survey result in each state",
                 subtitle = "The model's expectation averaged over each stream's actual surveys (10th-90th percentile across their conditions in brackets); traps per 100 trap-nights, burrows per 100 m, chew cards per card")
```

The ratios are what let a survey tell the states apart; the chance of finding nothing shows how often a single survey is uninformative. Because every detection term is shared by all states, the ratios are the same under any survey conditions for traps and burrows (on the log scale); for chew cards they hold on the odds scale.

How survey conditions change what each stream records, one subsection per data type: every detection term in that stream's formula. Everything else is held at one reference survey for that stream (each factor's most common level, numeric covariates at their median; 100 trap-nights or 100 m of transect), so these plots show each effect's shape; the gap between states is in the table above. A term shared by all states shifts every state by the same amount (on the log scale for traps and burrows, the log-odds scale for chew cards), so it is drawn once, at the low state's level. A term that differs between states is drawn in each state. Bands and bars are 95% intervals.

```{r}
#| label: detection-figures
#| results: asis

## One subsection per stream: its categorical terms, then its numeric terms (where it has any).
## Each figure is one column of panels, so its height (fig-asp) grows with its number of panels.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(stream_info))) {
  s <- stream_info$stream_label[i]
  child <- c(paste0("### ", stream_short[[s]]), "",
             "The submodel as specified in `_targets.R` (`hmm_observation_model`):", "",
             code_block(spec_code(stream_info$spec[i], hmm_observation_model[[stream_info$spec[i]]])),
             "Its estimated detection effects:", "")
  d <- filter(detection_effects, Stream == s)
  if (any(!d$numeric)) {
    n_panels <- length(unique(d$panel[!d$numeric]))
    child <- c(child, "```{r}", paste0("#| label: fig-detection-factors-", i),
               paste0("#| fig-cap: \"", stream_short[[s]], ": categorical detection terms, expected value (log scale; shared terms at the low state's level, state-specific terms in each state). Where a panel is split (e.g. by cropping system), the split is shown by point shape.\""),
               "#| fig-width: 7", paste0("#| fig-asp: ", round(0.6 * n_panels + 0.25, 2)), "",
               paste0("plot_detection_categorical(\"", s, "\")"), "```", "")
  }
  if (any(d$numeric)) {
    n_panels <- length(unique(d$panel[d$numeric]))
    child <- c(child, "```{r}", paste0("#| label: fig-detection-numeric-", i),
               paste0("#| fig-cap: \"", stream_short[[s]], ": numeric detection terms, expected value (log scale; shared terms at the low state's level, state-specific terms in each state). Where a panel is split (e.g. by soil group), the split is shown by line type.\""),
               "#| fig-width: 7", paste0("#| fig-asp: ", round(0.5 * n_panels + 0.3, 2)), "",
               paste0("plot_detection_numeric(\"", s, "\")"), "```", "")
  }
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = child, envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Transition submodels

Each transition has its own covariates, set by the season's conditions; one subsection per transition below. Each covariate is shown once. One with a single slope everywhere is a curve over its 5th-95th percentile; one whose slope differs by season, soil or AE zone has its own figure, a curve per season, soil group or zone; factors and 0/1 indicators are shown at each level. Everything else is held at its median, in `r reference_zone` (the zone closest to the average zone effects) on `r common_soil_group` soils. Bands and bars are 95% intervals.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-typical-rates

## Transition probabilities in a typical season, and the average stay in each state they imply.
typical_rates |>
  mutate(`Pr per season (95% interval)` = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(p), pct(lcl), pct(ucl))) |>
  select(Transition, `Pr per season (95% interval)`) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "A typical season",
                 subtitle = paste0("Every covariate at its median, in ", reference_zone, " on ", common_soil_group, " soils. Average stay: low ",
                                   round(stay_seasons[["Low"]], 1), ", medium ", round(stay_seasons[["Medium"]], 1), ", plague ",
                                   round(stay_seasons[["Plague"]], 1), " seasons"))
```

```{r}
#| label: transition-effects-prep
#| include: false

## Factor variables with their own effect in one transition's formula (soil group, season and 0/1 indicators as
## fixed effects, AE zone as a random intercept) -- not factors that only group a slope.
transition_factors <- function(from, to) {
  labels <- attr(stats::terms(stats::as.formula(plague_hmm$hid()$formula()[from, to])), "term.labels")
  ## 0/1 indicators with their own main effect (e.g. post_plague), shown as two levels.
  indicators <- labels[!grepl("[:(]", labels) & vapply(labels, function(l) l %in% names(hmm_data) && is_indicator(l), logical(1))]
  c(intersect(c("soil_group", "season"), labels), indicators, if (any(grepl("^s\\(ae_zone, bs", labels))) "ae_zone")
}
## Each factor level's transition probability, other covariates at their median (zone and soil as typical).
factor_effects <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(transition_factors(from, to), function(fv) {
    lvls <- switch(fv, soil_group = levels(hmm_data$soil_group), season = season_order, ae_zone = zone_levels, c("No", "Yes"))
    nd <- if (fv == "ae_zone") {
      dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(lvls, function(zn) transition_newdata("min_temp", stats::median(hmm_data$min_temp), zone = zn)))
    } else {
      transition_newdata("min_temp", rep(stats::median(hmm_data$min_temp), length(lvls)))
    }
    if (fv == "soil_group") {
      nd$soil_group <- factor(lvls, levels = lvls)
      nd$not_clay <- as.numeric(lvls != "cracking clay")
    }
    if (fv == "season") nd$season <- factor(lvls, levels = levels(hmm_data$season))
    ## A 0/1 indicator at 0 ("No") and 1 ("Yes").
    if (!fv %in% c("soil_group", "season", "ae_zone")) nd[[fv]] <- c(0, 1)
    p <- predict_ci("tpm", nd)
    tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = fv, level = lvls,
                   mle = p$mle[from, to, ], lcl = p$lcl[from, to, ], ucl = p$ucl[from, to, ])
  })
})

## Slopes that differ off cracking clay: each such covariate's curve on each soil group.
soil_slope_curves <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(soil_interaction_vars(from, to), function(cv) {
    values <- seq(stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 40)
    purrr::map_dfr(levels(hmm_data$soil_group), function(sg) {
      p <- predict_ci("tpm", transition_newdata(cv, values, soil = sg))
      tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = cv, soil_group = sg, value = values,
                     mle = p$mle[from, to, ], lcl = p$lcl[from, to, ], ucl = p$ucl[from, to, ])
    })
  })
})

## Season-dependent slopes: each covariate with a season interaction, a curve per season.
season_slope_vars <- function(from, to) {
  labels <- attr(stats::terms(stats::as.formula(plague_hmm$hid()$formula()[from, to])), "term.labels")
  sub("_scaled$", "", unique(sub(":?season:?", "", labels[grepl("(^|:)season(:|$)", labels) & grepl(":", labels)])))
}
season_slope_curves <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(season_slope_vars(from, to), function(cv) {
    values <- seq(stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 40)
    purrr::map_dfr(season_order, function(sn) {
      nd <- transition_newdata(cv, values)
      nd$season <- factor(sn, levels = levels(hmm_data$season))
      p <- predict_ci("tpm", nd)
      tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = cv, season = sn, value = values,
                     mle = p$mle[from, to, ], lcl = p$lcl[from, to, ], ucl = p$ucl[from, to, ])
    })
  })
})

## Slopes that vary by season and cropping system (partially pooled): each such covariate's curve in each
## season, for each cropping system.
season_crop_slope_vars <- function(from, to) {
  f <- plague_hmm$hid()$formula()[from, to]
  slopes <- regmatches(f, gregexpr("s\\(season, cropping_system, by = [a-z0-9_]+", f))[[1]]
  sub("_scaled$", "", sub("^s\\(season, cropping_system, by = ", "", slopes))
}
season_crop_slope_curves <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(season_crop_slope_vars(from, to), function(cv) {
    values <- seq(stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 40)
    purrr::map_dfr(levels(hmm_data$cropping_system), function(cs) {
      purrr::map_dfr(season_order, function(sn) {
        nd <- transition_newdata(cv, values)
        nd$season <- factor(sn, levels = levels(hmm_data$season))
        nd$cropping_system <- factor(cs, levels = levels(hmm_data$cropping_system))
        p <- predict_ci("tpm", nd)
        tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = cv, cropping_system = cs, season = sn, value = values,
                       mle = p$mle[from, to, ], lcl = p$lcl[from, to, ], ucl = p$ucl[from, to, ])
      })
    })
  })
})

## Zone-varying slopes: each such covariate's curve in every AE zone.
zone_slope_vars <- function(from, to) {
  f <- plague_hmm$hid()$formula()[from, to]
  slopes <- regmatches(f, gregexpr("s\\(ae_zone, by = [a-z0-9_]+", f))[[1]]
  sub("_scaled$", "", sub("^s\\(ae_zone, by = ", "", slopes))
}
zone_slope_curves <- purrr::pmap_dfr(transitions, function(from, to, label) {
  purrr::map_dfr(zone_slope_vars(from, to), function(cv) {
    values <- seq(stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), stats::quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 40)
    purrr::map_dfr(zone_levels, function(zn) {
      p <- plague_hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = transition_newdata(cv, values, zone = zn))
      tibble::tibble(transition = label, covariate = cv, ae_zone = zn, value = values, probability = p[from, to, ])
    })
  })
})

## Numeric covariates with one slope for every zone, season and soil: the others have figures of their own.
single_slope_vars <- function(from, to) {
  setdiff(transition_vars(from, to), c(zone_slope_vars(from, to), season_slope_vars(from, to), season_crop_slope_vars(from, to),
                                       soil_interaction_vars(from, to)))
}
## One transition's single-slope numeric covariates: a curve each, on its own panel.
plot_numeric_effects <- function(tr) {
  from <- transitions$from[transitions$label == tr]
  to <- transitions$to[transitions$label == tr]
  transition_curves |>
    filter(transition == tr, covariate %in% single_slope_vars(from, to)) |>
    mutate(covariate_label = factor(axis_label_of(covariate), levels = unique(axis_label_of(covariate)))) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, mle)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), fill = "grey40", alpha = 0.18) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season")) +
    strip_as_axis_title
}
## One transition's factor effects as plotted (also sizes the figure).
shown_factor_effects <- function(tr) {
  d <- filter(factor_effects, transition == tr)
  ## Where the transition has zone slopes, each zone's baseline is shown by its curve in the zone figure instead.
  from <- transitions$from[transitions$label == tr]
  to <- transitions$to[transitions$label == tr]
  if (length(zone_slope_vars(from, to)) > 0) d <- filter(d, covariate != "ae_zone")
  d
}
## One transition's factor covariates: soil group, 0/1 indicators and AE zone, a point and interval per level.
plot_factor_effects <- function(tr) {
  ## Levels ordered by probability within each factor (keyed by factor, so each panel keeps its own order).
  d <- shown_factor_effects(tr) |>
    mutate(covariate_label = factor(label_of(covariate), levels = unique(label_of(covariate)))) |>
    arrange(covariate_label, mle) |>
    mutate(level_key = factor(paste(covariate, level, sep = "|"), levels = unique(paste(covariate, level, sep = "|"))))
  ggplot(d, aes(mle, level_key)) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lcl, xmax = ucl), size = 0.3) +
    ## One column, each panel's height in proportion to its number of levels.
    ## Each panel's strip, left of its y axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_grid(covariate_label ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y", labeller = labeller(covariate_label = label_wrap_gen(20))) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = function(k) sub("^.*\\|", "", k)) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season"), y = NULL) +
    strip_as_axis_title
}
## One transition's soil-dependent slopes, by soil group.
plot_soil_slopes <- function(tr) {
  filter(soil_slope_curves, transition == tr) |>
    mutate(covariate_label = axis_label_of(covariate)) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, mle, colour = soil_group, fill = soil_group)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = soil_colours, name = "Soil group") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = soil_colours, name = "Soil group") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season")) +
    strip_as_axis_title +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
## One transition's season-dependent slopes, a curve per season (the season the conditions are measured in).
plot_season_slopes <- function(tr) {
  season_colours <- c(Summer = "#e41a1c", Autumn = "#ff7f00", Winter = "#377eb8", Spring = "#4daf4a")
  filter(season_slope_curves, transition == tr) |>
    mutate(covariate_label = axis_label_of(covariate), season = factor(season, levels = season_order)) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, mle, colour = season, fill = season)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), colour = NA, alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = season_colours, name = "Season measured") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = season_colours, name = "Season measured") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season")) +
    strip_as_axis_title +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
## One transition's season x cropping-system slopes: a curve per season, a panel per cropping system.
plot_season_crop_slopes <- function(tr) {
  season_colours <- c(Summer = "#e41a1c", Autumn = "#ff7f00", Winter = "#377eb8", Spring = "#4daf4a")
  crop_labels <- c(winter_cereal = "Winter cereal (winter-only)", sorghum = "Sorghum (summer + winter)")
  filter(season_crop_slope_curves, transition == tr) |>
    mutate(covariate_label = axis_label_of(covariate), season = factor(season, levels = season_order),
           cropping_system = factor(crop_labels[cropping_system], levels = crop_labels)) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, mle, colour = season, fill = season)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), colour = NA, alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title (the covariate, in one cropping system).
    facet_wrap(vars(covariate_label, cropping_system), scales = "free_x", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom",
               labeller = function(l) label_value(l, multi_line = FALSE)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = season_colours, name = "Season measured") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = season_colours, name = "Season measured") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season")) +
    strip_as_axis_title +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
## One transition's zone-varying slopes, a line per AE zone, with the average across zones in bold.
plot_zone_slopes <- function(tr) {
  d <- filter(zone_slope_curves, transition == tr) |> mutate(covariate_label = axis_label_of(covariate))
  ## The average across zones, on the logit scale the zone effects are added on.
  zone_average <- d |>
    group_by(covariate_label, value) |>
    summarise(probability = stats::plogis(mean(stats::qlogis(probability))), .groups = "drop")
  ## Each zone's name at the right-hand end of its curve, spread so labels don't overlap, in place of a legend.
  ends <- d |> group_by(covariate_label, ae_zone) |> slice_max(value, n = 1) |> ungroup()
  average_end <- zone_average |> group_by(covariate_label) |> slice_max(value, n = 1) |> ungroup()
  ggplot(d, aes(value, probability, colour = ae_zone)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = zone_average, aes(value, probability), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 1.4) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ends, aes(label = ae_zone), direction = "y", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.05 * diff(range(d$value)),
                             size = 3, segment.colour = "grey75", segment.size = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = average_end, aes(value, probability, label = "Average across zones"), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                             direction = "y", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.05 * diff(range(d$value)), size = 3, fontface = "bold",
                             segment.colour = "grey75", segment.size = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0) +
    ## One column; each panel's strip, below its x axis, is that axis's title.
    facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "turbo", guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.5))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season")) +
    strip_as_axis_title
}
## One transition's effect sizes: the transition probability at each numeric covariate's 10th and 90th percentile.
effect_size_table <- function(tr) {
  effect_sizes |>
    filter(transition == tr) |>
    arrange(desc(abs(change))) |>
    mutate(Covariate = label_of(covariate)) |>
    select(Covariate, `At 10th percentile` = low, `At 90th percentile` = high, Change = change) |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::fmt_percent(columns = -Covariate, decimals = 1) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em") |>
    gt::tab_header(title = paste("Effect sizes:", tr), subtitle = "Transition probability with the covariate at its 10th and 90th percentile, others at their median")
}

## One hypothesis table: "In model" lists the formula variables matching each row's pattern.
hypothesis_table <- function(tbl, from, to) {
  model_vars <- c(transition_vars(from, to), transition_factors(from, to))
  tbl |>
    mutate(`In model` = vapply(pattern, function(pt) {
      matched <- if (is.na(pt)) character(0) else grep(pt, model_vars, value = TRUE)
      if (length(matched) == 0) "--" else paste0("`", matched, "`", collapse = ", ")
    }, character(1))) |>
    select(Covariate, Reasoning, `In model`) |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `In model`) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
    gt::cols_width(Covariate ~ px(200), Reasoning ~ px(360), `In model` ~ px(200))
}

## The hypothesised drivers of each transition (starred: may vary spatially, by zone or soil type), and
## the hypothesis behind each transition. Rainfall anomalies are left out of the model where soil moisture
## covers the same window, since the two are nearly the same signal (r = 0.83).
## Low -> medium's 3-month GPP slope in each season the conditions are measured in (its slope plus that
## season's difference), for the summary below.
lm_coef <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()[, 1]
lm_gpp_slope <- vapply(season_order, function(se) {
  lm_coef[["S1>S2.gpp_rolling3_anomaly"]] + (if (se == season_order[1]) 0 else lm_coef[[paste0("S1>S2.gpp_rolling3_anomaly:season", se)]])
}, numeric(1))
lm_gpp_text <- paste0(
  "Good conditions measured in ", tolower(and_join(season_order[lm_gpp_slope > 0])), " raise build-up, as hypothesised",
  if (any(lm_gpp_slope < 0)) paste0("; good conditions in ", tolower(and_join(season_order[lm_gpp_slope < 0])), " lower it, which is not yet explained") else "",
  ".")
hypotheses <- list(
  `Low → medium` = list(
    summary = paste("A low population builds up when conditions turn good. The model measures the turn with the 3-month GPP anomaly (a 12-month window lags a drought break by up to a year), its effect differing by season, and the 12-month soil-moisture anomaly, differing on cracking clay.", lm_gpp_text),
    table = tibble::tribble(
      ~Covariate, ~Reasoning, ~pattern,
      "GPP anomaly (12-month)", "Positive: sufficient food (crop yield proxy). A 12-month window covers the whole cropping cycle, so it applies across dual and winter-only cropping systems.", "^gpp_anomaly$",
      "GPP anomaly (3-month), by season", "The turn to good conditions, measured over the season just ended; its effect may differ by season.", "^gpp_rolling3",
      "Rainfall anomaly (12-month)*", "Affects food and shelter. Effect likely varies regionally or by soil type.", "^rain_rolling12",
      "Soil-moisture anomaly (12-month)*", "Affects food and shelter. Effect likely varies regionally or by soil type.", "^soil_moisture_rolling12",
      "Cold nights (below 2 °C) in the last 12 months", "If it didn't get cold, breeding may not have paused and survival increases. A higher threshold may need testing.", "^min_temp_cold_days12"
    )),
  `Medium → plague` = list(
    summary = "A building-up population becomes a plague after a sharp swing from dry to wet conditions (rainfall whiplash), the key hypothesis. A plague doesn't start again within a year of the zone's last one ending: after a crash, densities are too low to respond, however good the conditions (the post-plague indicator, which in effect works as a rule). Other long-term candidates fitted where and when the few mapped plague onsets happened rather than forecasting earlier plague years, so they were left out.",
    table = tibble::tribble(
      ~Covariate, ~Reasoning, ~pattern,
      "Rainfall whiplash*", "A sharp swing from dry to wet conditions (Brown et al. 2026); the current key hypothesis.", "^rain_whiplash",
      "Recent plague in the zone", "After a plague crashes, densities are too low to erupt again straight away, even in good conditions.", "^post_plague$",
      "GPP anomaly (long-term)", "Consistently good food.", "^gpp_rolling36",
      "Rainfall anomaly (long-term)*", "Food and shelter resources.", "^rain_rolling36",
      "Soil-moisture anomaly (long-term)*", "Food and shelter resources.", "^soil_moisture_rolling36",
      "Cold nights (below 2 °C) in the last 12 months", "If it didn't get cold, breeding may not have paused over winter.", "^min_temp_cold_days12"
    )),
  `Medium → low` = list(
    summary = "A build-up fades when recent good conditions finish (previous 3-6 months).",
    table = tibble::tribble(
      ~Covariate, ~Reasoning, ~pattern,
      "Soil-moisture anomaly (recent)*", "Food and shelter resources.", "^soil_moisture_rolling6",
      "Cold temperatures", "Food and shelter resources.", "^min_temp_cold_days6",
      "GPP anomaly (recent)", "Food and shelter resources.", "^gpp_rolling6",
      "Rainfall anomaly (recent)*", "Food and shelter resources.", "^rain_rolling(3|6)_"
    )),
  `Plague → low` = list(
    summary = "A plague ends when the conditions behind it finish.",
    table = tibble::tribble(
      ~Covariate, ~Reasoning, ~pattern,
      "Rainfall whiplash", "The condition that caused the plague has finished.", "^rain_whiplash",
      "Minimum temperature", "Cold conditions stress mice.", "^min_temp",
      "Rainfall", "Waterlogging could make habitat unsuitable (soil moisture may represent this better).", "^rain_rolling(3|6)_",
      "Soil moisture*", "Affects burrowing capacity (habitat is limiting).", "^soil_moisture",
      "GPP", "Food runs out: current season or the last 6 months.", "^gpp",
      "Soil group and AE zone", "Baseline differences between soils and regions.", "^(soil_group|ae_zone)$"
    ))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: transition-subsections
#| results: asis

## One subsection per transition: its hypothesis, every covariate's effect (numeric curves, factor
## levels, soil- and zone-dependent slopes), its effect sizes and the hypothesis table.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(transitions))) {
  tr <- transitions$label[i]
  from <- transitions$from[i]
  to <- transitions$to[i]
  n_numeric <- length(transition_vars(from, to))
  n_single <- length(single_slope_vars(from, to))
  ## Every effect figure is one column of panels, so its height (fig-asp) grows with its number of panels.
  panel_asp <- function(n_panels, per_panel = 0.4, extra = 0.1) round(per_panel * n_panels + extra, 2)
  chunk <- function(label, caption, width, asp, code) {
    c("```{r}", paste0("#| label: ", label), paste0("#| fig-cap: \"", caption, "\""),
      paste0("#| fig-width: ", width), paste0("#| fig-asp: ", asp), "", code, "```", "")
  }
  key <- paste0(from, ">", to)
  child <- c(paste0("### ", tr), "", hypotheses[[tr]]$summary, "",
             "The submodel as specified in `_targets.R` (`hmm_transition_model`):", "",
             code_block(spec_code(paste0("`", key, "`"), hmm_transition_model[[key]])),
             "Its estimated effects:", "")
  if (n_single > 0) {
    child <- c(child, chunk(paste0("fig-numeric-", i),
      paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season as each numeric covariate with a single slope varies over its 5th-95th percentile, others at their median, in ", reference_zone, " on ", common_soil_group, " soils. Covariates whose slope varies by zone, season or soil are in the figures below."),
      7, panel_asp(n_single), paste0("plot_numeric_effects(\"", tr, "\")")))
  }
  if (length(transition_factors(from, to)) > 0) {
    child <- c(child, chunk(paste0("fig-factors-", i),
      paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season by each factor in its formula (soil group, season and 0/1 indicators as fixed effects, and AE zone as a random intercept where the zone figure doesn't already show it), other covariates at their median, in ", reference_zone, "."),
      7, round(0.06 * nrow(shown_factor_effects(tr)) + 0.1 * dplyr::n_distinct(shown_factor_effects(tr)$covariate) + 0.1, 2),
      paste0("plot_factor_effects(\"", tr, "\")")))
  }
  if (length(season_slope_vars(from, to)) > 0) {
    child <- c(child, chunk(paste0("fig-season-slopes-", i),
      paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season for the covariates whose slope differs by season, a curve per season the conditions are measured in (the transition is to the following season), other covariates at their median."),
      7, panel_asp(length(season_slope_vars(from, to)), extra = 0.2), paste0("plot_season_slopes(\"", tr, "\")")))
  }
  if (length(season_crop_slope_vars(from, to)) > 0) {
    child <- c(child, chunk(paste0("fig-season-crop-slopes-", i),
      paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season for the covariates whose slope varies by season and cropping system (one average slope plus partially-pooled deviations), a curve per season the conditions are measured in (the transition is to the following season), other covariates at their median."),
      7, panel_asp(2 * length(season_crop_slope_vars(from, to)), extra = 0.2), paste0("plot_season_crop_slopes(\"", tr, "\")")))
  }
  if (length(soil_interaction_vars(from, to)) > 0) {
    child <- c(child, chunk(paste0("fig-soil-slopes-", i),
      paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season for the covariates whose slope differs off cracking clay, by soil group (duplex/calcareous loam and sandy earth share a slope but not a baseline)."),
      7, panel_asp(length(soil_interaction_vars(from, to)), extra = 0.2), paste0("plot_soil_slopes(\"", tr, "\")")))
  }
  if (length(zone_slope_vars(from, to)) > 0) {
    child <- c(child, chunk(paste0("fig-zone-slopes-", i),
      paste0("Pr(", tolower(tr), ") per season for the covariates whose slope varies by zone, a line per AE zone (other covariates at their median) and the average across zones in bold. A line's height is that zone's baseline (its random intercept); its steepness is the zone's own slope, pulled towards the shared slope. The other figures for this transition are drawn in ", reference_zone, ", the zone closest to the average."),
      8, panel_asp(length(zone_slope_vars(from, to)), per_panel = 0.55), paste0("plot_zone_slopes(\"", tr, "\")")))
  }
  if (n_numeric > 0) {
    child <- c(child, "```{r}", paste0("#| label: tbl-effect-sizes-", i), "", paste0("effect_size_table(\"", tr, "\")"), "```", "")
  }
  child <- c(child, "::: {.callout-note collapse=\"true\"}", paste0("## Hypothesised drivers: ", tr), "",
             "\"In model\" is read from the fitted formula. Starred covariates may vary spatially, by zone or soil type.", "",
             "```{r}", paste0("#| label: tbl-hypotheses-", i), "", paste0("hypothesis_table(hypotheses[[\"", tr, "\"]]$table, ", from, ", ", to, ")"), "```",
             ":::", "")
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = child, envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Outputs

What the model produces: the current forecast and what drives it, the key covariates, and how earlier seasons look when the model is run back through the past (the hindcast).

### Current forecast

**The maps forecast `r forecast$target_season` `r forecast$target_year`**, from `r forecast$covariate_season` `r forecast$covariate_year` covariates (layer `r forecast$period`). Each cell's mix of low, medium and plague is carried forward season by season from the covariates alone (`r/e_hindcast_plague_occurrence.R`), then stepped one season ahead. They cover the prediction region: the fitted AE zones cut to SA2 cropping land plus 25 km around every surveyed paddock (`r/e_build_prediction_region.R`). The forecast reaches one season ahead only, since every covariate is built from observed data, and it doesn't yet use this season's surveys.

```{r}

Red where it is more likely than not, blue where less likely, white at 50%; dashed contour: 25%.")'
