#### What is driving the forecast

```{r}
#| label: drivers-prep
#| include: false

## One transition's mean contribution per zone and covariate, as a heatmap: zones ordered by the transition's
## zone-mean probability (in brackets), covariates in formula order with the baseline last.
plot_drivers <- function(tr) {
  d <- forecast_drivers[[tr]]
  covariate_order <- unique(label_of(c(setdiff(names(d), c("ae_zone", "risk", "baseline")), "baseline")))
  summary <- d |>
    group_by(ae_zone) |>
    summarise(risk = mean(risk), across(-risk, mean), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_longer(-c(ae_zone, risk), names_to = "covariate", values_to = "contribution") |>
    mutate(covariate = factor(label_of(covariate), levels = covariate_order),
           zone_label = paste0(ae_zone, " (", pct(risk), ")"))
  zone_order <- summary |> distinct(zone_label, risk) |> arrange(risk) |> pull(zone_label)
  limit <- max(abs(summary$contribution))
  ggplot(mutate(summary, zone_label = factor(zone_label, levels = zone_order)), aes(covariate, zone_label, fill = contribution)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f", contribution)), size = 2.8) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", limits = c(-limit, limit), name = "Push on logit risk") +
    labs(x = "Covariate", y = "AE zone (zone-mean probability)") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
}
```

Each covariate's push on the logit of Pr(medium → plague), averaged over each zone's cells (red raises risk, blue lowers it). Covariates are centred levels or anomalies, so zero means an average season; the baseline is the intercept, the soil group and the zone's own random intercept. Slopes that differ by season, soil or zone are included in their covariate's push. Zones are ordered by the zone-mean probability, in brackets.

```{r}
#| label: fig-forecast-drivers
#| fig-cap: "Why each zone's chance of a building-up population becoming a plague is what it is: pushes on the logit of Pr(medium → plague)."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.6

plot_drivers("Medium → plague")
```

The same breakdown for building up (low → medium) is in the Appendix (@fig-forecast-drivers-build-up).

### Key covariates

The covariates behind the forecast, as they stood at the end of `r forecast$covariate_season` `r forecast$covariate_year`: each transition covariate over its own window (its 3, 6 or 12 months to then), then the two main drivers over time. Rainfall whiplash drives medium → plague and the 3-month GPP anomaly drives low → medium.

```{r}
#| label: predictor-maps-prep
#| include: false

## The forecast period's end month, the last month of every covariate's window.
period_end <- as.Date(sprintf("%s-%s-15", sub(".*_", "", forecast$period), sub("_.*", "", forecast$period)))
## Each covariate's trailing window in months up to that month (r/b_compute_rolling_mean_raster.R): rolling
## anomalies over their own window, the season-end soil moisture and minimum temperature over the month and
## season, and rainfall whiplash's rise from its low over the last 12 months (r/b_compute_whiplash_raster.R).
covariate_window_months <- c(
  gpp_rolling3_anomaly = 3, gpp_rolling6_anomaly = 6, gpp_rolling6 = 6, gpp_anomaly = 12,
  soil_moisture_anomaly = 1, soil_moisture_rolling6_anomaly = 6, soil_moisture_rolling12_anomaly = 12,
  soil_moisture_rolling36_anomaly = 36, min_temp = 3, min_temp_cold_days12 = 12, rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak = 12
)
## A covariate's window in words, e.g. "Jun–Aug 2026 (winter)"; static covariates have none.
window_text <- function(cv) {
  n <- covariate_window_months[cv]
  if (is.na(n)) return("static")
  start <- seq(period_end, by = "-1 month", length.out = n)[n]
  span <- if (n == 1) format(period_end, "%b %Y") else if (format(start, "%Y") == format(period_end, "%Y")) {
    paste0(format(start, "%b"), "–", format(period_end, "%b %Y"))
  } else {
    paste0(format(start, "%b %Y"), "–", format(period_end, "%b %Y"))
  }
  ## A 3-month window is the season itself.
  if (n == 3) paste0(span, " (", tolower(forecast$covariate_season), ")") else span
}

## The transitions each covariate enters, from the model specification, in its order. not_clay modifies other
## covariates' slopes and post_plague is a zone indicator, so neither is mapped.
transition_terms <- purrr::imap_dfr(hmm_transition_model[!vapply(hmm_transition_model, identical, logical(1), "0")], function(terms_vec, key) {
  ij <- as.integer(strsplit(key, ">", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  covs <- unique(sub("_scaled$", "", unlist(lapply(terms_vec, function(t) all.vars(stats::as.formula(paste("~", t)))))))
  tibble::tibble(transition = paste(state_labels[ij[1]], "→", tolower(state_labels[ij[2]])), covariate = covs)
}) |>
  filter(covariate %in% names(covariate_rasters), !covariate %in% c("not_clay", "post_plague"))
mapped_covariates <- unique(transition_terms$covariate)
transitions_of <- function(cv) paste(transition_terms$transition[transition_terms$covariate == cv], collapse = "; ")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-predictor-maps
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Each transition covariate behind the ", forecast$target_season, " ", forecast$target_year, " forecast, over its own window to the end of ", forecast$covariate_season, " ", forecast$covariate_year, " (panel title), with the transitions it enters (subtitle). Each colour scale spans the middle 90% of that covariate\x27s values at the end of ", tolower(forecast$covariate_season), " across its record over the prediction region, with values beyond shown at the ends, so the colours show how this season compares with past ", tolower(forecast$covariate_season), "s. Anomalies are z-scores against the same time of year, red above average and blue below (white = average); rainfall whiplash is the 30-month rainfall z-score now minus its lowest point over the previous 12 months (negative where it is at a new low); minimum temperature is the season\x27s mean of daily minima (°C), shown again below as an anomaly against the same season\x27s mean at that place (display only).")'
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-asp: !expr 0.62 * (length(mapped_covariates) + ("min_temp" %in% mapped_covariates))

## Each covariate's layer for the forecast period (static soil group as is), masked to the prediction region.
region_vect <- terra::vect(prediction_region_ll)
period_month <- sub("_.*", "", forecast$period)
## A diverging scale with white at zero over limits lim, widened if needed so zero is always on the scale.
diverging_scale <- function(lim, name) {
  lim <- range(c(lim, 0))
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"), values = c(0, scales::rescale(0, from = lim), 1),
                       limits = lim, oob = scales::squish, name = name)
}
## A covariate panel: the map titled with its window, subtitled with the transitions it enters.
covariate_panel <- function(df, scale, title, subtitle) {
  grid_map(df, "value", scale, title) +
    labs(subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
          legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 8), legend.title.position = "top")
}
covariate_maps <- lapply(mapped_covariates, function(cv) {
  stack <- terra::mask(covariate_rasters[[cv]], region_vect)
  layer <- if (terra::nlyr(stack) == 1) stack else stack[[forecast$period]]
  df <- raster_df(layer, "value")
  if (cv == "soil_group") {
    ## Soil group: a categorical raster stored as labels or level positions.
    if (is.numeric(df$value)) df$value <- levels(hmm_data$soil_group)[df$value]
    scale <- scale_fill_manual(values = soil_colours, name = NULL)
  } else {
    ## Colour limits: the middle 90% of the covariate's values in the same season-end month across its record,
    ## inside the prediction region, so a season is judged against the same season in other years.
    same_season <- stack[[sub("_.*", "", names(stack)) == period_month]]
    lim <- unname(stats::quantile(terra::values(same_season, mat = FALSE), c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE))
    scale <- if (cv %in% c("min_temp", "gpp_rolling6")) {
      ## Levels: a sequential scale.
      scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = lim, oob = scales::squish, name = if (cv == "min_temp") "°C" else "gC/m²/day")
    } else {
      ## Anomalies and whiplash: diverging, white at zero (average; for whiplash, no change from its low).
      diverging_scale(lim, if (cv == "rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak") "Change (z-score units)" else "z-score")
    }
  }
  covariate_panel(df, scale, paste0(label_of(cv), ", ", window_text(cv)), transitions_of(cv))
})

## Minimum temperature as an anomaly too, below its level (display only; the model uses the level): each cell's
## value this season against its own mean and standard deviation for the same season across the record, as a
## z-score, so the map shows whether this season was warm or cold for that place.
if ("min_temp" %in% mapped_covariates) {
  min_temp_stack <- terra::mask(covariate_rasters$min_temp, region_vect)
  min_temp_seasons <- min_temp_stack[[sub("_.*", "", names(min_temp_stack)) == period_month]]
  min_temp_anomaly <- (min_temp_seasons - terra::app(min_temp_seasons, mean, na.rm = TRUE)) /
    terra::app(min_temp_seasons, stats::sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  ## Colour limits: the middle 90% of the anomaly across the record, as for the other panels.
  lim <- unname(stats::quantile(terra::values(min_temp_anomaly, mat = FALSE), c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE))
  anomaly_panel <- covariate_panel(raster_df(min_temp_anomaly[[forecast$period]], "value"), diverging_scale(lim, "z-score"),
                                   paste0("Minimum temperature anomaly, ", window_text("min_temp")),
                                   "Display only: the model uses the level above")
  covariate_maps <- append(covariate_maps, list(anomaly_panel), after = match("min_temp", mapped_covariates))
}
## One map per row.
patchwork::wrap_plots(covariate_maps, ncol = 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-key-covariates
#| fig-cap: "State means of rainfall whiplash (medium → plague) and the 3-month GPP anomaly (low → medium) at season end across the model's paddocks, with each state's recorded plague years shaded (none recorded for WA). Dashed line: start of anchoring (2013)."
#| fig-width: 10

state_names <- c(NSW = "New South Wales", QLD = "Queensland", SA = "South Australia", VIC = "Victoria", WA = "Western Australia")
key_covariates <- tibble::tibble(state = state_names[hmm_data$aus_state], x = lubridate::decimal_date(panel_dates),

ggplot(key_covariates, aes(x, value, colour = covariate)) +

            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.7) +
```

### Past seasons

Pr(medium) and Pr(plague) in every cell for earlier seasons, carried forward season by season from `r plague_hindcast$season[1]` `r min(plague_hindcast$year_adj)` through each season's transition matrix (`r/e_hindcast_plague_occurrence.R`). The grid uses the covariates only; the points are surveyed paddocks, coloured by their smoothed probability given their own survey data and anchors. Outlines are the hand-mapped plague extents for that season (Mutze 1989 for 1984).

```{r}
#| label: past-seasons-prep
#| include: false

## Years shown: the two most recent, then major recorded plague years, where the hindcast covers them.
hindcast_years <- sort(unique(plague_hindcast$year_adj))
past_years <- unique(c(rev(tail(hindcast_years, 2)), intersect(c(2021, 2017, 2011, 1993, 1984), hindcast_years)))

## Paddock points: surveyed paddock-seasons with their smoothed Pr(medium) and Pr(plague).
paddock_points <- tibble::tibble(longitude = hmm_data$longitude, latitude = hmm_data$latitude,
                                 year_adj = hmm_data$year_adj, season = as.character(hmm_data$season),
                                 Medium = state_probs[, "Medium"], Plague = state_probs[, "Plague"])[surveyed, ] |>
  pivot_longer(c(Medium, Plague), names_to = "State", values_to = "prob")

## Mapped plague extents with their season (Mutze's 1984 extents cover the whole year, so they're
## repeated in every 1984 season).
recent_extents <- recent_plague_maps |> st_transform(4326) |> st_make_valid()
mutze_1984_ll <- st_union(st_make_valid(st_transform(filter(mutze_plague_maps, year == 1984), 4326)))
extents <- rbind(
  st_sf(season = as.character(recent_extents$season), year = recent_extents$year, geometry = st_geometry(recent_extents)),
  st_sf(season = season_order, year = 1984, geometry = rep(mutze_1984_ll, length(season_order)))
)

## One year's maps: medium and plague in rows, seasons in columns.
past_year_map <- function(yr) {
  grid <- filter(plague_hindcast, year_adj == yr) |>
    select(x, y, season, Medium = state_2, Plague = state_3) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Medium, Plague), names_to = "State", values_to = "prob") |>
    mutate(season = factor(season, levels = season_order))
  ## The extents repeated for each row of panels.
  yr_extents <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Medium", "Plague"), function(st) mutate(filter(extents, year == yr), State = st))) |>
    mutate(season = factor(season, levels = season_order))
  pts <- filter(paddock_points, year_adj == yr) |> mutate(season = factor(season, levels = season_order))
  ## The mapped area's outline in each season with a hindcast, so a season not yet reached stays blank.
  outlines <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(as.character(grid$season)), function(se) {
    mutate(cell_outline(filter(grid, season == se)), season = factor(se, levels = season_order))
  }))
  ggplot() +
    geom_raster(data = grid, aes(x, y, fill = prob)) +
    geom_sf(data = outlines, fill = NA, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = yr_extents, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.45) +
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(longitude, latitude, fill = prob), shape = 21, size = 1.6, stroke = 0.3, colour = "black") +
    risk_scale +
    facet_grid(State ~ season, drop = FALSE) +
    coord_sf(xlim = range(grid$x) + c(-0.5, 0.5), ylim = range(grid$y) + c(-0.5, 0.5), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(fill = "Probability") +
    theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
```

### Hindcast against recorded plague years

```{r}
#| label: hindcast-prep

hindcast_first <- plague_hindcast |>
  filter(!is.na(onset)) |>
  distinct(year_adj, season) |>
  arrange(year_adj, match(season, season_order)) |>
  slice(1)
hindcast_n         <- get_hindcast("onset", "hindcast", "n")
hindcast_n_flagged <- get_hindcast("onset", "hindcast", "n_flagged")
anchored_n         <- get_hindcast("onset", "anchored era", "n")
anchored_n_flagged <- get_hindcast("onset", "anchored era", "n_flagged")
```

Before 2013 there are no anchors and almost no surveys, so plague years recorded by state in `yearly_plague_occurrence.csv` are labels the model never saw. The hindcast runs the transitions over every grid cell from `r hindcast_first$season` `r hindcast_first$year_adj` (`r/e_hindcast_plague_occurrence.R`); each state's cells are averaged, and the highest season in each year is scored against that state-year's record (`r/e_score_plague_hindcast.R`). Onset risk is Pr(plague next season | not plague now), each cell's medium → plague risk weighted by how likely it is to be in the medium state. The main score is the within-state AUC: flagged and unflagged years compared within the same state, so differences in baseline risk between states don't count.

```{r}
#| label: fig-hindcast-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "State-mean onset risk, Pr(plague next season | not plague now), highest season each year, with recorded plague years shaded. Dashed line: start of anchoring (2013)."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.9

hindcast_series <- plague_hindcast_scores$state_year
flagged_years <- distinct(filter(hindcast_series, flag == 1), state, year_adj)

ggplot(hindcast_series, aes(year_adj, onset_mean)) +
  geom_rect(data = flagged_years, aes(xmin = year_adj - 0.5, xmax = year_adj + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2012.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(colour = state_colours[["Plague"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, colour = state_colours[["Plague"]]) +
  facet_wrap(~state, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Onset risk, state mean")
```

```{r}
#| label: paddock-stories-prep
#| include: false

## Key paddocks: up to two per AE zone with the longest live-trapping records (at least 6 years trapped), plus,
## for any Australian state without one, its paddock with the most surveyed seasons.
trap_years <- hmm_data |>
  filter(!is.na(trap_count)) |>
  group_by(ID, year_adj) |>
  summarise(aus_state = first(aus_state), ae_zone = first(as.character(ae_zone)),
            longitude = first(longitude), latitude = first(latitude), .groups = "drop")
trapped_paddocks <- trap_years |>
  group_by(ID, aus_state, ae_zone) |>
  summarise(n = n(), first_year = min(year_adj), last_year = max(year_adj),
            longitude = first(longitude), latitude = first(latitude), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 6) |>
  group_by(ae_zone) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 2, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(what = "years trapped")
surveyed_paddocks <- hmm_data |>
  mutate(surveyed = surveyed) |>
  filter(surveyed, !(aus_state %in% trapped_paddocks$aus_state)) |>
  group_by(ID, aus_state, ae_zone = as.character(ae_zone)) |>
  summarise(n = n(), first_year = min(year_adj), last_year = max(year_adj),
            longitude = first(longitude), latitude = first(latitude), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(aus_state) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(what = "seasons surveyed")
## Panel label: zone, location and record (the data carry no site names).
key_paddocks <- bind_rows(trapped_paddocks, surveyed_paddocks) |>
  arrange(aus_state, ae_zone) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s, %s (%.2f, %.2f): %d %s, %d-%d", aus_state, ae_zone, longitude, latitude, n, what, first_year, last_year))
panel_levels <- key_paddocks$label

## Smoothed state probabilities at each key paddock, each season at its middle (a decimal year), stacked.
paddock_states <- tibble::tibble(ID = hmm_data$ID, x = lubridate::decimal_date(panel_dates),
                                 Low = state_probs[, "Low"], Medium = state_probs[, "Medium"], Plague = state_probs[, "Plague"]) |>
  inner_join(select(key_paddocks, ID, label), by = "ID") |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(state_labels), names_to = "layer", values_to = "value")
## Anchored seasons, as ticks above the probabilities: red plague, gold at least medium, green low, grey low or medium.
paddock_anchors <- tibble::tibble(ID = hmm_data$ID, x = lubridate::decimal_date(panel_dates), anchor = hmm_data$state) |>
  filter(!is.na(anchor)) |>
  inner_join(select(key_paddocks, ID, label), by = "ID") |>
  mutate(tick = case_when(anchor == "3" ~ state_colours[["Plague"]], anchor %in% c("2", "2,3") ~ state_colours[["Medium"]],
                          anchor == "1" ~ state_colours[["Low"]], TRUE ~ "grey55"))

## Each key paddock's hindcast grid cell (the nearest cell centre), and that cell's onset risk, highest season each
## year, drawn at the middle of the year.
hindcast_cells <- distinct(plague_hindcast, cell, x, y)
paddock_cell <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(key_paddocks)), function(i) {
  hindcast_cells$cell[which.min((hindcast_cells$x - key_paddocks$longitude[i])^2 + (hindcast_cells$y - key_paddocks$latitude[i])^2)]
}, numeric(1))
paddock_onset <- plague_hindcast |>
  filter(cell %in% paddock_cell, !is.na(onset)) |>
  group_by(cell, year_adj) |>
  summarise(onset = max(onset), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(tibble(cell = paddock_cell, label = key_paddocks$label), by = "cell", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(x = year_adj + 0.5)

## Each key paddock's surveys by year and stream: whether that stream surveyed the paddock that year, and whether its
## highest value was high -- trap success and burrows above the anchor thresholds that rule out the low state, and
## more than a quarter of chew cards chewed (chew cards don't anchor, so this cut-off is for display only).
chew_high_share <- 0.25
paddock_surveys <- hmm_data |>
  filter(ID %in% key_paddocks$ID) |>
  mutate(chew_share = rowMeans(as.matrix(across(all_of(chewcard_streams))), na.rm = TRUE) / 10) |>
  select(ID, year_adj, trap_success, burrows_per_transect, chew_share) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(ID, year_adj), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value), !is.nan(value)) |>
  group_by(ID, year_adj, measure) |>
  summarise(peak = max(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(layer = c(trap_success = "Live traps", burrows_per_transect = "Active burrows", chew_share = "Chew cards")[measure],
         high = case_when(measure == "trap_success"         ~ peak > anchor_trap_success_threshold,
                          measure == "burrows_per_transect" ~ peak > anchor_burrow_threshold,
                          .default                          = peak > chew_high_share),
         ## Survey rows under the probabilities, one per stream, each a tenth of the panel deep.
         row = match(layer, c("Live traps", "Active burrows", "Chew cards")),
         ymax = -0.02 - (row - 1) * 0.1, ymin = -row * 0.1) |>
  inner_join(select(key_paddocks, ID, label), by = "ID")

## One fill scale for the stacked states and the survey rows.
paddock_fills <- c(state_colours, `Live traps` = "grey20", `Active burrows` = "#8C5A2B", `Chew cards` = "#2B6C8C")
## The figure's height as a multiple of its 10-inch width: about two inches per paddock panel. (The report's
## default fig-asp overrides fig-height, so the height is set through fig-asp.)
paddock_fig_asp <- (2.2 * nrow(key_paddocks) + 1.2) / 10
## The figure's caption, built here since its thresholds come from the pipeline.
paddock_fig_caption <- sprintf("Key paddocks: the smoothed probability of each state given the paddock's own surveys and anchors (stacked; ticks above mark anchored seasons -- red plague, gold at least medium, green low, grey low or medium), against the onset risk, Pr(plague next season | not plague now), from the covariates alone at the paddock's grid cell (black line, highest season each year). Underneath, each year's surveys, one row per stream: solid where the year's highest value was high (trap success above %s%%, more than %s burrows per transect, or more than %s%% of chew cards chewed), faint where surveyed but not high, blank where not surveyed. Dashed line: start of anchoring (2013).", anchor_trap_success_threshold, anchor_burrow_threshold, 100 * chew_high_share)
```

### Key paddocks

The longest-surveyed paddocks (`r nrow(key_paddocks)`: up to two per AE zone with at least six years of live-trapping, plus the most-surveyed paddock in any state without one) tell the model's story at paddock scale. The stacked bands are what the model infers from the paddock's own surveys and anchors; the black line is what the covariates alone forecast, before any survey. Where the line rises ahead of the bands turning gold and red, the covariates gave warning; the survey rows underneath show what each stream found.

```{r}
#| label: fig-paddock-stories
#| fig-cap: !expr paddock_fig_caption
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-asp: !expr paddock_fig_asp

ggplot() +
  geom_area(data = mutate(paddock_states, layer = factor(layer, levels = rev(state_labels)), label = factor(label, levels = panel_levels)),
            aes(x, value, fill = layer), alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_rect(data = mutate(paddock_surveys, label = factor(label, levels = panel_levels)),
            aes(xmin = year_adj + 0.05, xmax = year_adj + 0.95, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = layer, alpha = high)) +
  geom_point(data = mutate(paddock_anchors, label = factor(label, levels = panel_levels)), aes(x, 1.05), colour = paddock_anchors$tick, shape = 124, size = 1.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2013, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = mutate(paddock_onset, label = factor(label, levels = panel_levels)), aes(x, onset), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 1, labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 110)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = paddock_fills, breaks = names(paddock_fills), name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.2, `TRUE` = 1), labels = c(`FALSE` = "surveyed", `TRUE` = "high"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(v) ifelse(v < 0, "", scales::percent(v)), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Probability") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), legend.position = "top")
```

## Model evaluation

How well the forecasts match what happened: skill against the recorded plague years the model never saw, consistency with the anchors at paddock level, calibration, and checks of the fitted distributions.

### Hindcast skill

```{r}
#| label: tbl-state-skill

                 subtitle = "AUC of each state's recorded plague years against its other years (0.5 = no skill)")
```

```{r}
hindcast_scores |>
  mutate(Predictor = recode(predictor, occupancy = "Occupancy", onset = "Onset, same year",
                            onset_lead = "Onset, one year ahead", rain_whiplash = "Rainfall whiplash alone"),
         Era = factor(recode(era, hindcast = "Before 2013 (unanchored)", `anchored era` = "2013 onwards (anchored)"),
                      levels = c("Before 2013 (unanchored)", "2013 onwards (anchored)")),
         `Within-state AUC (95% interval)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", auc_within, auc_within_lcl, auc_within_ucl),
         `Pooled AUC` = sprintf("%.2f", auc)) |>

  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Era") |>
```

- **Before 2013** (`r hindcast_n_flagged` flagged of `r hindcast_n` state-years), one-year-ahead onset scores `r fmt2(get_hindcast("onset_lead", "hindcast"))`, against `r fmt2(get_hindcast("rain_whiplash", "hindcast"))` for rainfall whiplash alone.
- **By state**, one-year-ahead AUC ranges from `r fmt2(min(state_skill$"Onset, one year ahead"))` (`r state_skill$state[which.min(state_skill$"Onset, one year ahead")]`) to `r fmt2(max(state_skill$"Onset, one year ahead"))` (`r state_skill$state[which.max(state_skill$"Onset, one year ahead")]`).
- **From 2013** only `r anchored_n_flagged` of `r anchored_n` state-years are flagged, and these years are anchored, so they check consistency rather than skill.
- **Caveats.** The records are coarse (a whole state, a calendar year, no WA), and the rainfall-whiplash definition was chosen partly against the same records.

```{r}
#| label: mutze-1984

## Spot check against Mutze's (1989) mapped 1984 SA plague extent: do SA cells inside it get higher
## 1984 onset risk than SA cells outside it?
mutze_1984 <- sf::st_union(sf::st_make_valid(filter(mutze_plague_maps, year == 1984)))
sa_outline <- filter(aus_shp, ST_NAME == "SA")
mutze_cells <- plague_hindcast |>
  filter(year_adj == 1984, !is.na(onset)) |>
  group_by(cell, x, y) |>
  summarise(onset = max(onset), .groups = "drop")
mutze_text <- if (nrow(mutze_cells) > 0) {
  pts <- sf::st_as_sf(mutze_cells, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = sf::st_crs(aus_shp))
  in_sa <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(pts, sa_outline)) > 0
  inside <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(pts, sf::st_transform(mutze_1984, sf::st_crs(pts)))) > 0
  d <- mutze_cells[in_sa, ]
  d$inside <- inside[in_sa]
  paste0("**Mapped 1984 SA plague (Mutze 1989).** ", sum(d$inside), " SA grain cells fall inside the mapped extent; their 1984 onset risk averages ",
         sprintf("%.3f", mean(d$onset[d$inside])), " against ", sprintf("%.3f", mean(d$onset[!d$inside])),
         " elsewhere in SA, a cell-level AUC of ", fmt2(hindcast_auc(d$onset, as.integer(d$inside))), ". One mapped extent, so a spot check rather than a skill score.")
} else {
  "**Mapped 1984 SA plague (Mutze 1989)** falls before the first hindcast season, so it can't be checked."
}
```

`r mutze_text`

### Onset skill at paddock level

```{r}
#| label: onset-skill

## For each paddock-season not anchored to plague, the model's one-step-ahead Pr(plague next season)
## given that paddock's data up to now (forward-filtered state probabilities times this season's
## transition matrix): does it separate paddocks whose next season is anchored to plague from those
## anchored not to be? The model was fitted to these anchors, so this checks consistency rather than
## out-of-sample skill.
log_forward <- plague_hmm$forward_backward()$logforward
filtered <- exp(sweep(log_forward, 2, apply(log_forward, 2, max)))
filtered <- sweep(filtered, 2, colSums(filtered), "/")
tpms <- plague_hmm$hid()$tpm(t = "all")
p_plague_next <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(filtered)), function(r) sum(filtered[, r] * tpms[, 3, r]), numeric(1))
eligible <- hmm_data |>
  mutate(p_next = p_plague_next) |>
  group_by(ID) |>
  mutate(next_anchor = lead(state)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ## Next season anchored to plague (onset) or to a non-plague set (stayed clear); now not anchored to plague.
  filter(next_anchor %in% c("3", "1,2", "2"), !(state %in% "3"))
onset <- eligible$next_anchor == "3"
## The same for one group of rows: all states, or one state (AUC blank without both onsets and seasons that stayed clear).
onset_summary <- function(rows, name) {
  o <- onset[rows]; p <- eligible$p_next[rows]
  tibble::tibble(Region = name, Onsets = sum(o), `Stayed clear` = sum(!o),
                 `Median Pr(plague next) before onset` = if (any(o)) median(p[o]) else NA_real_,
                 `Median Pr(plague next) before staying clear` = if (any(!o)) median(p[!o]) else NA_real_,
                 AUC = if (any(o) && any(!o)) auc_fn(p[o], p[!o]) else NA_real_)
}
## WA has no yearly plague records, so this check against its anchors is the only skill measure for it.
onset_skill <- onset_summary(rep(TRUE, nrow(eligible)), "All states")
onset_by_state <- purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(eligible$aus_state)), function(st) onset_summary(eligible$aus_state == st, st))
bind_rows(onset_by_state, onset_skill) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Region") |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(Onsets, `Stayed clear`)) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = starts_with("Median"), decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = AUC, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Paddock-level onset skill by state", subtitle = "Paddock-seasons not anchored to plague whose next season is anchored")
```

```{r}
#| label: operational-threshold

## The cutoff on Pr(plague next season) that best separates onsets from non-onsets (Youden's J).
roc_points <- purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(eligible$p_next)), function(th) {
  high <- eligible$p_next >= th
  tibble::tibble(threshold = th, sensitivity = mean(high[onset]), specificity = mean(!high[!onset]))
})
best_threshold <- roc_points |>
  mutate(youden = sensitivity + specificity - 1) |>
  slice_max(youden, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

Using each paddock's own surveys up to the season before, the model's Pr(plague next season) separates onsets from seasons that stayed clear with an AUC of `r fmt2(onset_skill$AUC)`; by state it ranges from `r fmt2(min(onset_by_state$AUC, na.rm = TRUE))` (`r onset_by_state$Region[which.min(onset_by_state$AUC)]`) to `r fmt2(max(onset_by_state$AUC, na.rm = TRUE))` (`r onset_by_state$Region[which.max(onset_by_state$AUC)]`). For WA, which has no yearly plague records, this is the only check of the forecast. A cutoff of **`r pct(best_threshold$threshold)`** separates them best, catching `r pct(best_threshold$sensitivity, 1)` of onsets while clearing `r pct(best_threshold$specificity, 1)` of seasons that stayed clear. It is a rough guide to where "elevated" starts on this model's scale, not an operational rule.

### Calibration

```{r}
#| label: calibration-prep

## Before vs after the surveys (r/e_check_plague_calibration.R): all regions per era, and the regions
## whose recent-era odds factor moves the forecast by more than 10%.
calib <- plague_calibration$before_after
calib_all <- calib[calib$region == "All regions", ]
calib_recent <- calib_all[grepl("onwards$", calib_all$era), ]
calib_early <- calib_all[!grepl("onwards$", calib_all$era), ]
recal <- plague_calibration$recalibration[plague_calibration$recalibration$region != "All regions", ]
over_regions <- recal$region[recal$factor < 0.9]
under_regions <- recal$region[recal$factor > 1.1]
## Brier skill: 1 minus the forecast's Brier score over the reference forecast's.
brier <- attr(plague_calibration$reliability, "brier")
brier_skill <- 1 - brier[["model"]] / brier[["reference"]]
chew_all <- plague_calibration$chew_zero[plague_calibration$chew_zero$region == "All regions", ]
```

A calibrated forecast gives, on average, the same chance before a paddock's surveys as after them. Across the surveyed paddock-seasons with no anchor, the chance of building up or plague averaged `r pct(calib_recent$before, 1)` before the surveys and `r pct(calib_recent$after, 1)` after them from `r calib_recent$era` (`r calib_recent$n` paddock-seasons). Before that it was `r pct(calib_early$before, 1)` before and `r pct(calib_early$after, 1)` after (`r calib_early$n`). The overall forecast is close, but regions differ (@tbl-calibration). `r if (length(over_regions) > 0) paste0("Recently the model has overstated the chance in ", and_join(over_regions), ". ") else ""``r if (length(under_regions) > 0) paste0("It has understated it in ", and_join(under_regions), ".") else ""` The chew cards agree: the forecast predicts `r pct(chew_all$predicted, 1)` of sessions finding no card chewed, against `r pct(chew_all$observed, 1)` observed.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-calibration
#| tbl-cap: "Mean chance of building up or plague before and after each season's surveys, at surveyed paddock-seasons with no anchor, by region and era; the recent-era odds factor that would bring the forecast in line with the surveys (shrunk towards 1 where there are few paddock-seasons; a diagnostic, not applied); and the share of chew-card sessions with no card chewed, predicted from the forecast against observed."

## One row per region: each era's before and after side by side, then the odds factor and chew-card zeros.
calib |>
  dplyr::rename(`Paddock-seasons` = n, Before = before, After = after) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = c(`Paddock-seasons`, Before, After), names_glue = "{era}_{.value}") |>
  left_join(dplyr::select(plague_calibration$recalibration, region, factor), by = "region") |>
  left_join(dplyr::rename(plague_calibration$chew_zero, chew_n = n, chew_predicted = predicted, chew_observed = observed), by = "region") |>
  ## All regions last.
  arrange(region == "All regions", region) |>
  dplyr::select(region, starts_with(calib_early$era), starts_with(calib_recent$era), factor, starts_with("chew_")) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "region") |>
  gt::tab_spanner_delim(delim = "_", columns = c(starts_with(calib_early$era), starts_with(calib_recent$era))) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Chew cards, none chewed", columns = starts_with("chew_")) |>
  gt::cols_label(factor = "Odds factor", chew_n = "Sessions", chew_predicted = "Predicted", chew_observed = "Observed") |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = c(ends_with("_Before"), ends_with("_After"), chew_predicted, chew_observed), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = factor, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = c(ends_with("_Paddock-seasons"), chew_n)) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

Against the plague maps, the paddock-level forecast of plague next season is reliable across its range (@fig-reliability), with a Brier score of `r sprintf("%.3f", brier[["model"]])` against `r sprintf("%.3f", brier[["reference"]])` for always forecasting the overall mapped plague share (Brier skill `r fmt2(brier_skill)`). The model was fitted to these maps, and much of the skill comes from plague persisting from one mapped season to the next, so this checks consistency rather than out-of-sample skill.

```{r}
#| label: fig-reliability
#| fig-cap: "Forecast Pr(plague next season) at mapped paddock-seasons, binned, against the share the map recorded as plague. Points on the dashed line are calibrated; point size is the number of paddock-seasons."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-asp: 0.9

ggplot(plague_calibration$reliability, aes(forecast, observed)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(colour = state_colours[["Plague"]]) +
```

Randomised quantile residuals (`r/e_randomised_pseudores.R`) compare each observation with the model's one-season-ahead forecast of it; for a well-specified model they are standard normal (mean 0, SD 1, about 5% beyond ±2).

## Limitations

```{r}
#| label: limitations-stats

## Near-singular joint precision (from collinear terms) makes the uncertainty sampling fall back to a
## generalised inverse; reported only if it occurs.
ev <- eigen(as.matrix(plague_hmm$tmb_rep()$jointPrecision), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
cond_number <- max(ev) / min(ev)
## Soil groups with few paddocks, whose interaction coefficients rest on little data.
soil_paddocks <- hmm_data |> distinct(ID, soil_group) |> count(soil_group)
thin_soil <- soil_paddocks$soil_group[soil_paddocks$n == min(soil_paddocks$n)]
```

- **Weak warning in the north.** `r if (length(weak_states) > 0) paste0("Before 2013, one-year-ahead onset risk does little better than chance in ", and_join(weak_states), " (@tbl-state-skill).") else "Hindcast skill is similar across states (@tbl-state-skill)."`
- **The medium state is only partly anchored.** Maps say where plague is and isn't; only survey counts mark a season as at least medium or as not plague, using thresholds (`r anchor_trap_success_threshold`% and `r anchor_trap_low_threshold`% trap success, `r anchor_burrow_threshold` burrows per transect, `r anchor_trap_low_min_effort` trap-nights) that are first guesses. Nothing anchors the low state on its own.
- **Few independent plague events.** The medium → plague transition rests on `r nrow(mapped_seasons)` mapped plague seasons; it improves only as more seasons are mapped.
- **Mapped plagues count once per paddock.** A mapped season anchors every surveyed paddock inside it, so one mapped event in a heavily surveyed zone weighs far more than a plague recorded at a few long-term trapping sites.
- **Post-plague window chosen in-sample.** The one-year window of the post-plague indicator was set by looking at the same yearly records the hindcast is scored against, so part of its skill gain is in-sample.
- **Soil-dependent slopes contrast cracking clay with every other soil.** `r tools::toTitleCase(as.character(thin_soil))` soils cover only `r min(soil_paddocks$n)` of `r sum(soil_paddocks$n)` paddocks (nearly all in WA), too few for slopes of their own, so they share duplex/calcareous loam's.
- **One season ahead, covariates only.** The covariates are observed data, so the forecast can't extend beyond the season after the latest complete covariate period, and the gridded forecast doesn't yet use the current season's surveys.
- **Regional bias.** `r if (length(over_regions) + length(under_regions) > 0) paste0("The forecast is calibrated overall but not in every region (@tbl-calibration)", if (length(over_regions) > 0) paste0(": it has recently overstated the chance in ", and_join(over_regions)) else "", if (length(under_regions) > 0) paste0(if (length(over_regions) > 0) " and understated it in " else ": it has recently understated the chance in ", and_join(under_regions)) else "", ". The odds factors are shown as a diagnostic, not applied.") else "Recent forecasts are calibrated in every region (@tbl-calibration)."`
- **Coarse validation before 2013.** The hindcast is scored against state-by-year records with no WA coverage, and no anchors exist before `r first_mapped_year`.
- **Imperfect count distributions.** `r if (length(ppc_outside) > 0) paste0("Simulated data miss the ", and_join(ppc_label(ppc_outside)), ".") else "Simulated data match the checked statistics."`
- **Survey grids sharing coordinates.** Some sites surveyed two grids or transects on the same dates under one set of coordinates; cleaning keeps one of each pair, which can favour the busier grid (`r/a_clean_deduplicate_surveys.R`).
- **Patched hmmTMB.** The beta-binomial family comes from a patched hmmTMB (github.com/matt-w-rees/hmmTMB, pinned in `renv.lock`).
- `r if (cond_number > 1e12) paste0("**Near-singular precision matrix** (condition number ", formatC(cond_number, format = "e", digits = 1), "): the uncertainty sampling falls back to a generalised inverse, which can understate interval widths along the affected directions.") else "**Uncertainty sampling** uses a well-conditioned precision matrix."`

## Future directions

Outstanding jobs and ideas worth trying, grouped by the part of the model they touch.

**Transitions**

- **Frost-risk nights on low → medium.** Cold, dry nights (minimum below 2 °C with low morning vapour pressure) as a driver of build-up, by season and possibly by zone. Plain cold nights didn't forecast build-up, but frost-risk nights are a different, rarer signal. The code is written (`r/b_count_silo_frost_days.R`); it needs the historical SILO vapour-pressure files downloaded.
- **Regional spread on medium → plague.** Whether a plague nearby last season (the zone in plague, or mapped plague within about 100 km) makes a building-up population more likely to tip over: the mirror image of the post-plague term. Screen with the expected transitions first; judge on the hindcast, since shared anchors make it look strong in-sample.
- **What drives plague in WA Sandplain.** Its plague starts follow no measure of rainfall whiplash, current or lagged. Once more WA seasons are mapped, screen other drivers there (GPP, soil moisture, the crop cycle).
- **Too much build-up after strong winter-cereal winters.** The forecast chance of building up in spring after a very strong winter crop is higher than spring surveys imply; the real rise comes a year later. A term for the previous crop's size, timed to the following autumn and winter, may capture it.
- **Northern summer crops.** A GPP window matched to the sorghum cropping calendar for build-up in the north, where winter-cereal timing fits poorly.

**Detection**

- **Rain after a dry spell on cracking clay.** Burrows seem easier to see when an unusually wet month follows two or more dry ones, but on about 60 surveys; revisit as clay surveys accumulate.
- **Sandy-earth burrow slopes.** Sandy earth shares duplex/calcareous loam's rain slope for burrows; give it its own once there are more WA burrow surveys.
- **Paddock-scale GPP for traps.** GPP at the trap month, which exists for every trapping session (crop stage is missing for most historic ones), as a canopy covariate for traps.
- **Crop stage by crop for summer crops.** Young and old summer crops may differ in burrow visibility, but there are too few northern surveys to estimate it yet.

**Anchoring and data**

- **Mapped plagues count once per paddock.** One mapped season in a heavily surveyed zone outweighs a plague recorded at a few long-term trapping sites. Weighting each mapped season as a fixed number of events, or anchoring fewer paddocks per mapped region, would balance them.
- **Survey grids sharing coordinates.** Some sites surveyed two grids under one set of coordinates; cleaning keeps one of each pair, which can favour the busier grid. Grid coordinates, or a rule that keeps the in-crop grid, would fix it.
- **Anchor thresholds.** The trap and burrow thresholds were checked against the model's own count distributions and kept; revisit as anchoring changes.

## Appendix

### Specification

Every term below is read from the model specification in `_targets.R` (`hmm_observation_model`, `hmm_transition_model`), so these tables always match the fitted model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spec-observation

## One row per observation term: its stream, family, parameter and how it is treated across states.
family_names <- c(nbinom2 = "Negative binomial", betabinom = "Beta-binomial", binom = "Binomial", zibinom = "Zero-inflated binomial")
term_treatment <- function(term, state_specific) {
  if (term == "1") return("Intercept only: one value per state")
  if (grepl("^offset\\(", term)) return("Offset: coefficient fixed at 1 (per unit of search effort)")
  if (any(all.vars(stats::as.formula(paste("~", term))) %in% state_specific)) return("Separate value in each state")
  "Shared by all states (detection effect)"
}
purrr::imap_dfr(hmm_observation_model, function(spec, stream) {
  params <- setdiff(names(spec), c("family", "state_specific", "tied_states"))
  purrr::map_dfr(params, function(param) {
    terms_vec <- spec[[param]]
    rows <- tibble::tibble(Term = terms_vec, Treatment = vapply(terms_vec, term_treatment, "", state_specific = spec$state_specific))
    ## Every parameter with covariates also has an intercept, one value per state.
    if (!identical(terms_vec, "1")) rows <- bind_rows(tibble::tibble(Term = "(intercept)", Treatment = "One value per state"), rows)
    mutate(rows, Stream = if (stream == "chewcard") "chewcard (all four blocks, every coefficient shared)" else stream,
           Family = family_names[[spec$family]], Parameter = param)
  })
}) |>
  mutate(Term = paste0("`", Term, "`")) |>
  select(Stream, Family, Parameter, Term, Treatment) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Stream") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = Term) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Observation model")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spec-transition

## One row per transition term, with what it means.
term_meaning <- function(term) {
  if (term == "0") return("Ruled out")
  if (grepl("^s\\(ae_zone, by", term)) return(paste0("AE-zone random slope on ", sub("^s\\(ae_zone, by = ([^,]+),.*$", "\\1", term)))
  if (grepl("^s\\(ae_zone", term)) return("AE-zone random intercept")
  if (grepl(":", term)) {
    parts <- strsplit(term, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if ("season" %in% parts) return("Slope differs by season")
    if (any(c("not_clay", "cracking_clay") %in% parts)) return("Slope differs off cracking clay")
    return("Interaction")
  }
  if (term == "post_plague") return("Indicator: the zone came out of a plague within the last year (r/e_build_zone_plague_history.R)")
  if (grepl("_scaled$", term)) return("Level, centred and scaled (r/e_scale_covariates.R)")
  if (grepl("anomaly", term)) return("Anomaly against the same time of year")
  if (term == "soil_group") return("Soil group (factor)")
  "Fixed effect"
}
purrr::imap_dfr(hmm_transition_model, function(terms_vec, key) {
  ij <- as.integer(strsplit(key, ">", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  tibble::tibble(Transition = paste(state_labels[ij[1]], "→", state_labels[ij[2]]), Term = terms_vec)
}) |>
  mutate(Meaning = vapply(Term, term_meaning, ""), Term = ifelse(Term == "0", "--", paste0("`", Term, "`"))) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Transition") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = Term) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Transition model", subtitle = "This season's covariates set the transition to next season's state")
```


### Transition coefficients

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coeff

## Fixed-effect transition coefficients (logit scale), one column per estimated transition.
cf <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()
tibble::tibble(Parameter = rownames(cf), Estimate = cf[, 1]) |>
  mutate(key = sub("^S([0-9])>S([0-9])\\..*$", "\\1>\\2", Parameter),
         Term = sub("^S[0-9]>S[0-9]\\.", "", Parameter)) |>
  ## Ruled-out transitions are fixed intercepts, not estimates.
  filter(!vapply(key, function(k) identical(hmm_transition_model[[k]], "0"), logical(1))) |>
  mutate(Transition = vapply(strsplit(key, ">"), function(ij) paste(state_labels[as.integer(ij[1])], "→", state_labels[as.integer(ij[2])]), "")) |>
  select(Transition, Term, Estimate) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Transition") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = Estimate, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Transition fixed effects (logit scale, against staying in the same state)",
                 subtitle = "\"_scaled\" covariates are per standard deviation; rainfall whiplash is the pooled slope, zone deviations below")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-zone-effects

## Zone random effects: intercept deviations per transition, and each zone's total rainfall-whiplash slope.
re <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_re()
fe <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()
rn <- rownames(re)
is_slope <- grepl(":rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak_scaled\\.[0-9]+$", rn)
key <- sub("^S([0-9])>S([0-9])\\..*$", "\\1>\\2", rn)
tibble::tibble(
  Transition = vapply(strsplit(key, ">"), function(ij) paste(state_labels[as.integer(ij[1])], "→", state_labels[as.integer(ij[2])]), ""),
  ae_zone    = zone_levels[as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", rn))],
  Effect     = ifelse(is_slope, "whiplash slope", "intercept deviation"),
  ## A zone's total whiplash slope adds the transition's pooled slope to the zone deviation.
  value      = re[, 1] + vapply(seq_along(rn), function(i) {
    if (!is_slope[i]) return(0)
    fe[paste0(sub("^(S[0-9]>S[0-9])\\..*$", "\\1", rn[i]), ".rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak_scaled"), 1]
  }, numeric(1))
) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Transition, Effect), values_from = value, names_sep = ": ") |>
  rename(`AE zone` = ae_zone) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = -`AE zone`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.72em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "AE-zone effects on the transitions (logit scale)",
                 subtitle = "Intercept deviations from each transition's pooled intercept, and each zone's total rainfall-whiplash slope")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-risk-zones

risk_by_zone |>

  arrange(desc(`Plague | mean`)) |>
  rename(`AE zone` = ae_zone) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = -`AE zone`, decimals = 1) |>

```

### Forecast detail

The two steps towards a plague, mapped for a paddock already in the starting state. They aren't forecasts on their own: the forecast weights each by how likely a cell is to be in the starting state now.

```{r}
#| label: fig-transition-maps
#| fig-cap: "The two steps towards a plague, for a paddock already in the starting state: Pr(low → medium) (left) and Pr(medium → plague) (right)."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-asp: 0.4

patchwork::wrap_plots(
  grid_map(raster_df(plague_build_up_map, "risk"), "risk", risk_scale, "Low → medium"),
  grid_map(raster_df(plague_risk_map, "risk"), "risk", risk_scale, "Medium → plague"),
  ncol = 2, guides = "collect"
) & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Each covariate's push on the logit of Pr(low → medium), averaged over each zone's cells (red raises risk, blue lowers it). Covariates are centred levels or anomalies, so zero means an average season; the baseline is the intercept, the soil group and the zone's own random intercept. Slopes that differ by season, soil or zone are included in their covariate's push. Zones are ordered by the zone-mean probability, in brackets.

```{r}
#| label: fig-forecast-drivers-build-up
#| fig-cap: "Why each zone's chance of building up is what it is: pushes on the logit of Pr(low → medium)."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.6

plot_drivers("Low → medium")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map-uncertainty
#| fig-cap: "Width of the 95% interval for Pr(medium → plague), on the logit scale (a probability-scale width looks small whenever risk is near 0% or 100%, however uncertain the estimate). From 500 posterior draws of the model's coefficients. Darker = less certain."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-asp: 0.6

## Logit written out, since stats::qlogis() doesn't accept a SpatRaster but raster arithmetic does.
logit <- function(p) log(p / (1 - p))
width <- logit(plague_risk_map_uncertainty[["ucl"]]) - logit(plague_risk_map_uncertainty[["lcl"]])
grid_map(raster_df(width, "logit_width"), "logit_width",
         scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Purples", direction = 1, name = "95% interval width (logit)"))
```


### Adjusted AE zones

The burrow and chew-card zone effects use `r length(adj_zone_levels)` adjusted AE zones, merging AE zones with few surveys (`r/a_adjust_aez.R`); the transitions keep all `r length(zone_levels)` original AE zones.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-obs-zones

hmm_data |>
  group_by(`Adjusted AE zone` = ae_zone_adj) |>
  summarise(`AE zones` = paste(sort(unique(as.character(ae_zone))), collapse = ", "),
            `Burrow surveys` = sum(!is.na(burrow_count)), `Chew-card surveys` = sum(!is.na(chewcard_count)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```
